en_US.LOC_PEDIA_CIVILIZATIONS_PAGE_CIVILIZATIO: The history of a unified Tibet begins with the rule of Songtsen Gampo (604–650 CE), who united parts of the Yarlung River Valley and founded the Tibetan Empire. He also brought in many reforms, and Tibetan power spread rapidly, creating a large and powerful empire. It is traditionally considered that his first wife was the Princess of Nepal, Bhrikuti, and that she played a great role in the establishment of Buddhism in Tibet. In 640 he married Princess Wencheng, the niece of the powerful Chinese emperor Taizong of Tang China, who herself was also Buddhist. The faith grew when an influx of Central Asian Buddhists flooded Tibet early in the eighth century, fleeing from advancing armies of Arab and Kazakh Muslims. Songtsen Gampo’s descendants would also conquer the vast region that is now the Chinese provinces of Qinghai, Gansu, and Xinjiang between 663 and 692. Control of these border regions would change hands back and forth for centuries to come.

Chinese power waxed strong in the early decades of the eighth century, and Imperial forces under General Gao Xianzhi conquered much of Central Asia, until their defeat by the Arabs and Karluks at the Battle of Talas River in 751. China's power quickly waned, and Tibet resumed control of much of Central Asia. Led by Trisong Detsen, the ascendant Tibetans pressed their advantage, conquering much of northern India and even seizing the Tang Chinese capital city of Chang’an (now Xi’an) in 763. Tibet and China signed a peace treaty in 821 or 822, which delineated the border between the two empires. The Tibetan Empire would concentrate on its Central Asian holdings for the next several decades, before splitting into several small, fractious kingdoms.

Canny politicians, the Tibetans befriended Genghis Khan just as the Mongol leader was conquering the known world in the early 13th century. As a result, though the Tibetans paid tribute to the Mongols after the Hordes had conquered China, they were allowed much greater autonomy than the other Mongol-conquered lands. Over time, Tibet came to be considered one of the thirteen provinces of the Mongolian-ruled nation of Yuan China. During this period, the Tibetans gained a high degree of influence over the Mongols at court. The great Tibetan spiritual leader, Sakya Pandita, became the Mongol's representative to Tibet. Sakya's nephew, Chana Dorje, married one of the Mongol Emperor Kublai Khan's daughters. The Tibetans transmitted their Buddhist faith to the eastern Mongols; Kublai Khan himself studied Tibetan beliefs with the great teacher Drogon Chogyal Phagpa.

When the Mongols' Yuan Empire fell in 1368 to the ethnic-Han Chinese Ming, Tibet reasserted its independence and refused to pay tribute to the new Emperor. In 1474, the abbot of an important Tibetan Buddhist monastery, Gendun Drup, passed away. A child who born two years later was found to be a reincarnation of the abbot, and was raised to be the next leader of that sect, Gendun Gyatso. After their lifetimes, the two men were called the First and Second Dalai Lamas. Their sect, the Gelug or “Yellow Hats”, became the dominant form of Tibetan Buddhism. The Third Dalai Lama, Sonam Gyatso (1543-1588), was the first to be so named during his life. He was responsible for converting the Mongols to Gelug Tibetan Buddhism, and it was the Mongol ruler Altan Khan who probably gave the title “Dalai Lama” to Sonam Gyatso. While the newly-named Dalai Lama consolidated the power of his spiritual position, though, the Gtsang-pa Dynasty assumed the royal throne of Tibet in 1562. The Kings would rule the secular side of Tibetan life for the next 80 years.

During the 1630s, China was embroiled in power struggles between the Mongols, Han Chinese of the fading Ming Dynasty, and the Manchu people of north-eastern China (Manchuria). The Manchus would eventually defeat the Han in 1644, and establish China's final imperial dynasty, the Qing (1644-1912). Tibet got drawn into this turmoil when the Mongol warlord Ligdan Khan, a Kagyu Tibetan Buddhist, decided to invade Tibet and destroy the Yellow Hats in 1634. Ligdan Khan died on the way, but his follower Tsogt Taij took up the cause. The great general Gushi Khan, of the Oirad Mongols, fought against Tsogt Taij and defeated him in 1637. The Khan killed the Gtsang-pa Prince of Tsang, as well. With support from Gushi Khan, the Fifth Dalai Lama, Lobsang Gyatso, was able to seize both spiritual and temporal power over all of Tibet in 1642.

The Potala Palace in Lhasa was constructed as a symbol of this new synthesis of power. The Dalai Lama made a state visit to the Qing Dynasty's second Emperor, Shunzhi, in 1653. The two leaders greeted one another as equals; the Dalai Lama did not kowtow. Each man bestowed honors and titles upon the other, and the Dalai Lama was recognized as the spiritual authority of the Qing Empire. Lobsang Gyatso died in 1682, but his Prime Minister concealed the Dalai Lama's passing until 1696 so that the Potala Palace could be finished and the power of the Dalai Lama's office consolidated.

In 1697, fifteen years after the death of Lobsang Gyatso, the Sixth Dalai Lama was finally enthroned. Tsangyang Gyatso (1683-1706) was a maverick who rejected the monastic life, growing his hair long, drinking wine, and enjoying female company. He also wrote great poetry, some of which is still recited today in Tibet. The Dalai Lama’s unconventional lifestyle prompted Lobsang Khan of the Khoshud Mongols to depose him in 1705. Lobsang Khan seized control of Tibet, named himself King, sent Tsangyang Gyatso to Beijing (he “mysteriously” died on the way), and installed a pretender Dalai Lama.

King Lobsang would rule for 12 years, until the Dzungar Mongols invaded and took power. They killed the pretender to the Dalai Lama’s throne, to the joy of the Tibetan people, but then began to loot monasteries around Lhasa. This vandalism brought a quick response from the Qing Emperor Kangxi, who sent troops to Tibet. The Dzungars destroyed the Imperial Chinese battalion near Lhasa in 1718. In 1720, the angry Kangxi sent another, larger force to Tibet, which crushed the Dzungars. The Qing army also brought the proper Seventh Dalai Lama, Kelzang Gyatso (1708-1757) to Lhasa. Qing China had its hands full trying to control Tibet. The Emperor sent a commissioner to Lhasa, but he was killed in 1750. The Imperial Army then defeated the rebels, but the Emperor recognized that he would have to rule through the Dalai Lama rather than directly. Day-to-day decisions would be made on the local level.

Qing Chinese power waned throughout the eighteenth century, as evidenced by its defeat in the Opium Wars with Britain (1839-1842 and 1856-1860), as well as the Taiping Rebellion (1850-1864) and the Boxer Rebellion (1899-1901). The actual relationship between China and Tibet had been unclear since the early days of the Qing Dynasty, and China's losses at home made the status of Tibet even more uncertain. The ambiguity of control over Tibet lead to problems. In 1893, the British in India concluded a trade and border treaty with Beijing concerning the boundary between Sikkim and Tibet. However, the Tibetans flatly rejected the treaty terms. The British invaded Tibet in 1903 with 10,000 men, and took Lhasa the following year. Thereupon, they concluded another treaty with the Tibetans, as well as Chinese, Nepalese and Bhutanese representatives, which gave the British themselves some control over Tibet’s affairs.

The 13th Dalai Lama, Thubten Gyatso, fled the country in 1904 at the urging of his Russian disciple, Agvan Dorzhiev. He went first to Mongolia, then made his way to Beijing. The Chinese declared that the Dalai Lama had been deposed as soon as he left Tibet, and claimed full sovereignty over not only Tibet but also Nepal and Bhutan. The Dalai Lama went to Beijing to discuss the situation with the Emperor Guangxu, but he flatly refused to kowtow to the Emperor. He returned to Lhasa in 1909, disappointed by Chinese policies towards Tibet. China sent a force of 6,000 troops into Tibet, and the Dalai Lama fled to Darjeeling, India later that same year. The Chinese Revolution swept away the Qing Dynasty in 1911, and the Tibetans promptly expelled all Chinese troops from Lhasa. The Dalai Lama returned home to Tibet in 1912.

Representatives of Great Britain, China, and Tibet met in 1914 to negotiate a treaty marking out the boundary lines between India and its northern neighbors. China walked out of the conference without signing the treaty after Britain laid claim to the Tawang area of southern Tibet, which is now part of the Indian state of Arunachal Pradesh. Tibet and Britain both signed the treaty. Soon, China would be too distracted to concern itself with the issue of Tibet. The new government of the Republic of China would hold nominal power over the majority of Chinese territory for only four years before war broke out between numerous armed factions. Under such circumstances, the Chinese showed little interest in Tibet. The 13th Dalai Lama ruled independent Tibet in peace until his death in 1933.

Following Thubten Gyatso's death, the new reincarnation of the Dalai Lama was born in Amdo in 1935. Tenzin Gyatso, the current Dalai Lama, was taken to Lhasa in 1937 to begin training for his duties as the leader of Tibet. In 1950, the newly-formed People's Republic of China invaded Tibet. With stability reestablished in Beijing for the first time in decades, Mao Zedong sought to assert China's right to rule over Tibet as well. The PLA inflicted a swift and total defeat on Tibet's small army, and China drafted the “Seventeen Point Agreement” incorporating Tibet as an autonomous region of the People's Republic of China. Representatives of the Dalai Lama's government signed the agreement under protest, and the Tibetans repudiated the agreement nine years later.

On March 1, 1959, the Dalai Lama received an odd invitation to attend a theater performance at PLA headquarters near Lhasa. PLA officers notified the Dalai Lama's bodyguards that they would not accompany the Tibetan leader to the performance, nor were they to notify the Tibetan people that he was leaving the palace. (Ordinarily, the people of Lhasa would line the streets to greet the Dalai Lama each time he ventured out.) The guards immediately publicized this rather ham-handed attempted abduction, and the following day an estimated crowd of 300,000 Tibetans surrounded Potala Palace to protect their leader. The PLA moved artillery into range of major monasteries and the Dalai Lama's summer palace, Norbulingka. Both sides began to dig in, although the Tibetan army was much smaller than its adversary, and poorly armed. Tibetan troops were able to secure a route for the Dalai Lama to escape into India on March 17. Actual fighting began on March 19, and lasted only two days before the Tibetan troops were defeated.

en_US.LOC_PEDIA_DISTRICTS_PAGE_DISTRICT_SUK_DZ: Dzongs are type of fortress found in Tibet and Bhutan. These towering structures are characterised by their enormity, with towering exterior walls surrounding a complex of courtyards, temples, administrative offices, and monks’ accommodations. Frequently located on a hilltop or mountain spur, Dzongs are constructed without the use of architectural plans. Instead construction proceeds under the direction of a high lama who establishes each dimension by means of spiritual inspiration.

In Tibet, Dzongs were integrated into the administration of the country. According to some sources it was Jangchub Gyaltsen (1302-73) who pioneered the Tibetan system of dividing vast territorial holdings into districts, each administered from a Dzong. When Jangchub Gyaltsen replaced the “thirteen myriarchies”, he divided the land into numerous districts (also called Dzong). He appointed those men among his followers, who were of unquestioned loyalty, to be masters (Dzongpon) of the districts. In modern Tibet, most Dzongs are lost or in ruins, with only a few restored as museums. It is only in Bhutan that we find the Dzongs still alive today as administration centers and monasteries.

en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MODIFIER_SUK_ENLIGHTENED_LORD_: Trisong Detsen admires your high Faith and your Golden Age
Trisong Detsen is disgusted by your lack of Faith and ambition
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_SUK_TRISONG_DETS: You rule the windswept steppes, Trisong Detsen. You rule the soaring mountains. Let bells ring in lofty monasteries as monks pray for your glory. Let the earth tremble as your mighty horsemen ride to war. Enlightened Lord, may you find wisdom in the Dharma and strength in the bow, that Tibet may climb to eternity.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DECLARE_FRIEND_FROM_AI_LEADER_: Join me in friendship! Together we will be a spiritual paragon for the world!
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_REJECT_DECLARE_FRIEND_FROM_HUM: No. I don't think so.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_ACCEPT_DECLARE_FRIEND_FROM_HUM: Yes, this is a worthy suggestion.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DECLARE_WAR_FROM_AI_LEADER_SUK: My horsemen will trample your fields. Prepare for your doom!
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DECLARE_WAR_FROM_HUMAN_LEADER_: Surely our bows and our devotion to the Dharma shall protect us from harm! We do not fear you.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DEFEAT_FROM_AI_LEADER_SUK_TRIS: I do not fear the end. My good Karma will ensure a auspicious rebirth.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DELEGATION_FROM_AI_LEADER_SUK_: I have sent a trade delegation. They come bearing butter tea. Drink up!
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_REJECT_DELEGATION_FROM_HUMAN_L: Ah, you have unfortunate timing. I am currently preoccupied with overseeing the construction of a Stupa. Perhaps next time.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_ACCEPT_DELEGATION_FROM_HUMAN_L: Thank you for your fine gifts. We will cherish them.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DENOUNCE_FROM_AI_LEADER_SUK_TR: Truly pathetic. Spiritually dull, and with no worldly accomplishments of note.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DENOUNCE_FROM_HUMAN_LEADER_SUK: Such foul words. They reveal your foul heart.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_FIRST_MEET_LEADER_SUK_TRISONG_: Blessings, and welcome to Tibet. I am Trisong Detsen, lord and Emperor of these lands.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_FIRST_MEET_VISIT_RECIPIENT_LEA: A famed monk is holding a lecture on the Dharma. Please come join us.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_FIRST_MEET_NEAR_INITIATOR_POSI: I thank you for your hospitality.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_FIRST_MEET_NO_MANS_INFO_EXCHAN: My capital is hidden, high in the mountains. I will tell you more if you tell me about your capital.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_WARNING_EXIT_LEADER_SUK_TRISON: No devotion and no ambition. How can you rule with neither spiritual or worldly excellence?
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_KUDO_EXIT_LEADER_SUK_TRISONG_D: Your achievements on this earth are no doubt the fruits of your great Karma. Truly worthy of praise.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MAKE_ALLIANCE_FROM_AI_LEADER_S: I am loath to tie Tibet to other nations, but this seems a wise course of action for us both. What say you?
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_ACCEPT_MAKE_DEAL_FROM_AI_LEADE: I will have my monks bless this agreement.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MAKE_PEACE_AI_ACCEPT_DEAL_LEAD: Peace. And a respite to all this death.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MAKE_PEACE_AI_REFUSE_DEAL_LEAD: No! Tibet is not ready to make peace.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MAKE_PEACE_FROM_AI_LEADER_SUK_: My monks suggest I seek peace for my people's spiritual well-being.

en_US.LOC_PEDIA_LEADERS_PAGE_LEADER_SUK_TRISON: Tight compact mountainous cities: this is how Tibet should build. And with the aid of some religious devotion, they will excel. Trisong Detsen takes Tibet’s religious infrastructure and readies it for war.

Tibet is a nation of mountain strongholds and monasteries: building districts near mountains not only provides extra yields, but also allows you to purchase buildings in those districts with [ICON_Faith] Faith. With help from your [ICON_Governor] Governors and your Dzong, you should have plenty of [ICON_Faith] Faith to do just that. Trisong Detsen takes Tibet’s formidable religious infrastructure and readies it for war. Build Encampment districts wherever you have Dzongs to earn [ICON_GreatGeneral] Great Generals faster and train stronger units.

Among the most celebrated figures in Tibetan history are the “Dharma Kings” (Chögyal in Tibetan) who supported Buddhism and helped it to take root in Tibet. And probably the most important of all the Dharma Kings is Trisong Detsen. The Tibetan empire that the young Trisong Detsen inherited was in serious decline. After the glorious reign of King Songtsen Gampo, the first Dharma King of Tibet, the empire was disintegrating as Tibet lost several cities in Turkestan, Nepal became embroiled in a rebellion, and the Arabs began encroaching on the Western front of the Tibetan empire.

Trisong Detsen reversed this tide, and undertook military campaigns to ensure Tibet’s expansion. In 763 Trisong Detsen sent an army of 200,000 men to the border with Tang China, defeating the forces there and then continuing on to take Chang'an, the Tang Chinese capital, forcing Emperor Daizong of Tang to flee the capital. In 783 a peace treaty was negotiated between China and Tibet giving Tibet all lands in Qinghai. Trisong Detsen also sought to expand westward, reaching the Amu Darya and threatening the Abbasid Caliph, Harun ar-Rashid. The Caliph was concerned enough to establish an alliance with the Chinese emperor. King Trisong Detsen would be preoccupied with Arab wars in the west, taking pressure off his Chinese opponents to the east and north, until his rule ended in 797.

However, he is best remembered by later generations of Tibetan Buddhists for his great patronage of Buddhism. When Trisong Detsen became emperor in 755 and, he invited Padmasambhava, Śāntarakṣita, Vimalamitra, and various other Indian teachers to come to Tibet to spread the latest understanding of the teaching. The two pandits began by establishing Samye as the first Buddhist monastery in Tibet. Several Tibetans were eventually initiated as monks and a vast translation project was undertaken translating the Buddhist scriptures from Sanskrit into Classical Tibetan.

It was not just the Indian branch of Buddhism that made its way into Tibet during Trisong Detsen’s reign. The first documented dissemination of Chan Buddhism to Tibet, chronicled in what has become known as the Statements of the Sba Family, occurred in about 761 when Trisong Detsen sent a party to the Yizhou region to receive the teachings of Kim Hwasang, a Korean Chan master, who they encountered in Sichuan. The party received teachings and three Chinese texts from Kim, who died soon after. Trisong Detsen patronised a second party to China in 763. This second expedition was headed by a high minister, Sba Gsalsnan. There is scholarly dissent about whom Gsalsnan encountered in Yizhou. Early scholarship considered Kim, but this had been revised to Baotang Wuzhu (714-774), head and founder of Baotang Monastery in Chengdu.

The two branches of Buddhism finally came to a head. Trisong Detsen, hosted a famous two-year debate from 792-794, known in Western scholarship as the “Council of Lhasa” (although it took place at Samye at quite a distance from Lhasa) outside the capital. He sponsored a Dharma debate between the Chan Buddhist Moheyan, who represented the third documented wave of Chan dissemination in Tibet, and the scholar Kamalaśīla, a student of Śāntarakṣita. Effectively the debate was between the Chinese and Indian Buddhist traditions as they were represented in Tibet. Sources differ about both the nature of the debate as well as the victor.

Trisong Detsen retired to live at the palace at Zungkar and handed power to his second son, Muné Tsenpo, in 797. From this point there is much confusion in the various historical sources. It seems there was a struggle for the succession after the death of Trisong Detsen. It is not clear when Trisong Detsen died, or for how long Mune Tsenpo reigned. The Testament of Ba, a Tibetan historical text which may date back to the 9th century, claims that Muné Tsenpo insisted that his father's funeral be performed according to Buddhist rather than traditional rites.

en_US.LOC_PEDIA_UNITS_PAGE_UNIT_SUK_JAHAZI_CHA: The largest traditional sailing vessel in wide use off the coast of East Africa is the jahazi, which measures up to 20m long and whose large billowing sails are a characteristic sight off Zanzibar and other traditional ports. With a capacity of about a hundred passengers, the jahazi is mainly used for transporting cargo and passengers over relatively long distances or in open water, for instance between Dar es Salaam and Zanzibar. Minor modifications in the Portuguese and Omani eras notwithstanding, the design of the modern jahazi is pretty much identical to that of similar seafaring vessels used in medieval times and before. The name jahazi is generally applied to boats with cutaway bows and square sterns built on Zanzibar and nearby parts of the mainland.

en_US.LOC_PEDIA_BUILDINGS_PAGE_BUILDING_SUK_PI: One of the most distinctive and enigmatic architectural forms associated with the Swahili were the structures associated with burials. The remains of monumental tomb structures still litter the coastal regions and mark many of the long-vanished centers of Swahili life. The simplest tomb structures were rectangular enclosures, bounded by four low walls, varying in size and scale. The most distinctive and unusual feature of many Swahili medieval tombs was the addition of a tall column-like structure, forming a characteristic building type along the East African coast referred to as pillar tombs. These pillars come in many sizes and shapes, from rounded, square, multisided or fluted and rose to various heights. These pillars, and sometimes parts of the surrounding enclosure walls, were often decorated with inset porcelain or other glazed ceramic bowls imported from southern Arabia, Persia and even as far as China, adding a dash of color to contrast with the brilliant white plaster surfaces, forming a distinctive decorative tradition unique to the medieval East African coast.

en_US.LOC_PEDIA_CIVILIZATIONS_PAGE_CIVILIZATIO: The medieval sites along the Swahili Coast represent a single cultural tradition with diverse local traditions that can be traced to the ninth century, which is considered to have developed into the modern Swahili culture. Currently, there are 173 identified settlements that flourished along the Swahili Coast and nearby Islands from the ninth to the seventeenth centuries, which include the sites of Kilwa, Malindi, Gedi, Pate and Comoros.

Wa-swahili, or “shore people”, designates the inhabitants of the East African coastline, and signifies above all a culture with a common language, Kiswahili, and the same religion, Islam. Arab-Persian geographers referred to the inhabitants of the East African coast as the Zanj. It was at the beginning of the nineteenth century that the first use of the term “Swahili” appeared, with settlers trying to classify and differentiate the different populations of Africa. The Swahilis have defined themselves as such since the colonial period, but differentiate between themselves according to their region, island or town of origin. Despite some common ground, Swahili identity remains multiple, incorporating populations of diverse background, both Cushitic and Bantu.

At the beginning of the first millenium CE, the discovery of the monsoon winds and the means to use them created a nautical revolution, allowing for major water crossings toward India and Ceylon. From the ninth century onward, Muslim geographers mention regular trade relations with East Africa, Pemba and Sofala. These sources indicate that as early as the ninth century, there were major shipping routes between Asia and Africa.

As a result of this burgeoning trade, the transition between the eleventh and twelfth century was a period of change. A number of urban East African centers developed at this time as did architecture in stone, used for public buildings, mosques and enclosure walls. The Swahili city-states were established. By the thirteenth century, a new balance of power had developed. The Swahili coast was divided into several independent sultanates, including Kilwa, Mombasa, Malindi, Pate and Mogadishu.

Kilwa was supposedly one of the most beautiful towns in the world with stone houses covered with palm-leaf roofs or makuti; only certain mosques and the palace had hard flat roofs. From the fourteenth to fifteenth century, Kilwa continued to hold the monopoly for gold, trading gold from Yufi, situated a one-month walk from the coast. Sofala, a vassal of Kilwa city, maintained commercial relations with the Shona kingdom of Great Zimbabwe; the rise of Great Zimbabwe was intimately linked to the trading of gold with Islamized peoples.

The arrival of the Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama in 1498 signaled a new era of foreign rule on the Swahili Coast. On a mission to economically control and Christianize the Swahili coast, the Portuguese attacked Kilwa first in 1505 and other cities later. Because of Swahili resistance, the Portuguese attempt at establishing commercial control was never successful. By the late 17th century, Portuguese authority on the Swahili coast began to diminish. With the help of Omani Arabs, by 1729 the Portuguese presence had been removed. The Swahili coast eventually became part of the Sultanate of Oman. Trade recovered, but it did not regain the levels of the past.

The Swahili civilization stands at the periphery of the Muslim and African worlds, resulting in the development of a unique coastal culture based on trade. In fact, its marginal position is linked to our vision of the Indian Ocean, which separates Africa, Arabia and Asia. But the ocean also provides a connection between these very different cultures: the Swahilis are thus dynamic players, equal to Arab, Persian and Indian traders. Swahili archaeology is at the crossroads of Islamic archaeology and African archaeology.

en_US.LOC_PEDIA_LEADERS_PAGE_LEADER_SUK_AL_HAS: Though perhaps not masters of naval warfare, the Swahili excel at thriving on the coast. Al-Hasan's abilities buffs the Swahili's most important district: the Harbor.

Unlike England, Norway, and Spain, the Swahili have almost no bonuses to enhance their naval might. What they do have is the potential for a strong and versatile economic base that those other naval civs would envy. Build your cities on the coast and keep them compact to maximise the benefit you get from your unique ability and the Pillar Tomb. Under al-Hasan, you won't have to worry about fresh water either: your Harbors can act as an excellent substitute, and give culture to boot! If you're ever short on [ICON_Production] Production in your coastal cities, train or buy some Jahazis and send them where they're needed. The most important thing to remember is to not neglect your navy, or your cities may fall prey to the likes of Norway.

Sultan al-Hasan ibn Sulaiman, often referred to as “Abu’l-Mawahib” (“father of gifts”), was the ruler of the city-state of Kilwa, from 1310 until 1333. Much of what we know about al-Hasan and about Kilwa itself comes to us through the writings of Ibn Battuta, an extremely well travelled Muslim scholar.

Ibn Battuta recorded his visit to the city around 1331, and commented favorably on the humility and religion of al-Hasan. Sultan al-Hasan ibn Sulaiman is reported to have have been a generous and intelligent man. He passed several years studying the sciences (ilm) at Mecca, where he became, “erudite and learned.” Ibn Battuata was extemely impressed by the sultan’s generosity, noting that he would sit and dine with beggars, and was very liberal with distributing gifts to all (including Ibn Batutta himself) who came to see him. It is because of this generosity that al-Hasan earned the epithet “Father of Gifts.”

Ibn Battuta was also particularly impressed by the planning of the city and believed that it was the reason for Kilwa’s success along the coast. During al-Hasan’s reign, Kilwa saw the construction of the Palace of Husuni Kubwa. The site, built of jagged blocks of coral called coral rag, is now only accessible from a worn staircase carved out of the cliff leading up from the water. Its ruin includes traditional Swahili elements, such as a stepped greeting court bordered by guest rooms for visiting merchants, and elements borrowed from other Islamic palaces, such as an octagonal swimming pool, grand audience court, and a residence with some 100 rooms. But the sultan had overreached in his ambition: The palace was occupied for only a short time before it was abandoned, unfinished.

Also during his reign, the sultan made a significant extension to the Great Mosque of Kilwa, which was made of coral stones—the largest mosque of its kind. He built an extension from the east wall of the northern prayer hall, which wrapped around forming a large open court. A very narrow barrel vaulted corridor, consisting of 30 bays complete with dressed coral panels and supported by coral columns ran directly southward. This extension juts out slightly to the east, creating a wing that deviates from the otherwise orthogonal plan. Within the space where the wall splays, two small irregular rooms were preceded by a small porch containing a tank filled with smooth quartz pebbles, a sandstone foot-rubber and a bench. Behind this small assembly of rooms is a somewhat larger plainly vaulted room. This long room leads into a square room four meters across which carries the great dome. This dome, noted in the Kilwa Chronicle, is thought to be the first true dome on Africa’s east coast. It was supported on squinches and decorated with dressed coral panels. After his visit in 1331, Ibn Battuta remarked on the splendor of the dome, which was, until the nineteenth century, the largest dome on the East African coast.

en_US.LOC_DEMO_COMPLETE_CONTENT: Congratulations! You have taken the first steps towards building a Civilization to stand the test of time. Will you continue to test yourself against the greatest leaders of history? Can your people’s culture flourish? Your science enlighten? Your faith inspire? Your military dominate?[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]How will you lead in Sid Meier’s Civilization VI? Continue the journey now.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Build. Conquer. Inspire.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_ACCEPT_DECLARE_FRIEND_FROM_AI_: Wonderful, I must send the good news to the Cantons at once!
What a fine day! May this become the start of something wonderful.
This will bring us both much fortune.
Nothing is left for me to do but to offer you my sincerest thanks.
I look forward to our people's futures together, as friends.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_ACCEPT_DECLARE_FRIEND_FROM_HUM: It pleases me greatly that out people can make this declaration!
The pleasure would be all mine.
Ich stimme zu, unsere Freundschaft der Welt zu erklären. (I accept your offer of friendship.)
I will honour your wish, for it is one shared by the Gods.
Excellent.
Excellent.
I would gladly link arms with a fellow lover of freedom.
Consider it settled!
I would be proud to call you friend.
I see no reason to deny.
I look forward to our future as friends.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_ACCEPT_DELEGATION_FROM_HUMAN_L: Your delegation has been welcomed by the Cantons with open arms!
I gladly accept. Your delegates are welcome to stay and enjoy their time in Malacca.
Ich akzeptiere deine Delegation mit Freude! (I accept your delegation with joy.)
I will speak with them.
Argentina is grateful for your kindness
Fine.
I accept your kind gifts.
Your delegates will be treated well and with esteem, I assure you.
Thank you, this offering is nicely decorated. I'll make sure to visit your lands some day.
Your delegate will be granted a new complex, and will be gifted servants and guards that I have chosen myself. It is an honor.
Your delegation is more welcome, we shall treat them as we treat our own.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_ACCEPT_MAKE_DEAL_FROM_AI_LEADE: This will do nicely, thank you.
This will bring us both much fortune.
Excellent! I shall have it drafted at once.
I look forward to our people's futures together, as friends.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_ACCEPT_OPEN_BORDERS_FROM_HUMAN: By all means, an open borders arrangement would be most beneficial.
Of course, please enjoy your time here.
Ja, ich bin damit einverstanden, meine Grenzen für Ihre kleinen Soldaten zu öffnen. (Yes I agree to open my borders to your little soldiers.)
May it prove our good fortune.
I accept your request.
I accept your request.
Friends of freedom are always welcome here.
Agreed! I cannot wait to hear of the fabulous riches of your lands.
Excellent! Such vast new lands to explore.
Your soldiers are allowed, and will be guided by ceremonial warriors. As befits their station.
I agree to these terms.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DECLARE_FRIEND_FROM_AI_LEADER_: Your nation and its people are a great inspiration and example to us, and in gratitude, I offer Switzerland's friendship to you.
You are a gifted ruler who knows the value of good relations. I formally extend to you my hand in friendship.
Es wäre in Eurem Interesse, dass Ihr dieses Angebot sorgfältig prüft. (It would be in your best interest, to carefully consider this proposal of friendship.)
I believe we must come to terms with the will of the Gods. We are destined to be friends, and we need only to declare it.
I'm happy to consider you a friend. Do you think the same?
Your people are civilized. Argentina could benefit from a Friendship with you.
My best friend is one who rights my wrongs and reproaches my mistakes. Would you like to be that person?
Perhaps I could tempt you with a written declaration of friendship?
Comply.
It is piqujait! I will gladly join you.
My priests agree that the stars are right. Oxhuitzá asks for your friendship.
Our people have a shared connection which should be formalised for it to grow.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DECLARE_WAR_FROM_AI_LEADER_CVS: Let it be known, I did not want this war. However, you have forced my hand and rendered it the only option.
I take no pleasure in this decision, but you have forced my hand. Your tyranny ends here.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DECLARE_WAR_FROM_AI_LEADER_GED: Verderbter Bösewicht! Wir werden Euch unter die Erde bringen! (Corrupted villain! We will bring you into the ground!)
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DECLARE_WAR_FROM_AI_LEADER_JFD: The Gods give me strength. We march to war.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DECLARE_WAR_FROM_AI_LEADER_LEU: I do this for my people!
Let this day be remembered, for today starts my great conquest of the lands I own but you're standing upon.

The time of tyrants has passed! I made a sacred promise that if liberty should ever be attacked, I would claim the honor of defending the freedom of those oppressed; and now the time has come to make good on that promise.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DECLARE_WAR_FROM_AI_LEADER_LIM: The price of peace has become far too great. It is time to bring Ba'al's storm down upon you!
You are backward and weak-willed and scared of the wild. Now you see what it brings you. Now you meet the storm.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DECLARE_WAR_FROM_AI_LEADER_LL_: You are a blind ruler. You could not see the stars, nor my armies, nor my plots come into place. Now, the Great Star calls for war!
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DECLARE_WAR_FROM_AI_LEADER_MER: I had not wanted to undertake such a responsibility as leadership during war, but you have forced my hand.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DECLARE_WAR_FROM_HUMAN_LEADER_: You fool. We are not a warlike people, but the fact that our small nation stands tall should have indicated to you that we are far from helpless. That ignorance shall be your downfall.
I applaud your bravery, but your intelligence leaves much to be desired.
Ich kann nicht warten bis Ihr noch mächtiger geworden seid. Bereitet Euch also auf den Krieg vor! (I cannot wait until ye grow even mightier. Therefore, prepare for war!)
I dreamt of this moment. I did not end with your victory.
I always knew you were up to something. My people will defend their lands with their hearts!
At last! Some action!
Your coarse impudence in making me employ my sword in war is simply incomprehensible. You insolent scoundrel, you will come to rue this decision!
Then you too shall be humbled before the walls of Byblos!
Amusing.
This is not a war. This is an adventure! One that will make a fine story of how aggressors shall always be defeated.
The Red Star is out of your favor, and the Great Star does not pour water. This will not take long.
You will find my soldiers have the utmost confidence in my leadership, and will not waiver in their duty to fight for their home, faith and country.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DEFEAT_FROM_AI_LEADER_CVS_ESCH: I may fall, but Switzerland has been occupied and freed in the past. Make no mistake, we will return and prosper once again.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DEFEAT_FROM_AI_LEADER_CVS_ISKA: Today you may have glory, but tomorrow you will come sooner than you think.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DEFEAT_FROM_AI_LEADER_GEDEMO_B: Deutschland ist zerstört worden. Ich weine um die zukünftigen Generationen. (Germany has been destroyed. I weep for the future generations.)
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DEFEAT_FROM_AI_LEADER_LEU_EVIT: Don't cry for me, Argentina... The truth is, I never left you, all through my wild days, my mad existence I kept my promise... Don't keep your distance.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DEFEAT_FROM_AI_LEADER_LEU_ROCA: I can't believe my people lost to you brutes! But know that nothing stands in the path of progress!
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DEFEAT_FROM_AI_LEADER_LEU_SANM: This is the exhaustion of death… I only regret not having anything else to sacrifice to the desire of contributing to the freedom of my country.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DEFEAT_FROM_AI_LEADER_LIME_PHO: Our business is concluded. I do hope you have no complaints, but in all honesty I don't particularly care.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DEFEAT_FROM_AI_LEADER_LIME_TEO: You may have won. For now.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DEFEAT_FROM_AI_LEADER_LIME_THU: I suppose this is it. My last adventure. The last obstacle I couldn't overcome, it was you in the end. I can feel my heart beating slower, and now I turn to stone. I feel cold... so cold...
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DEFEAT_FROM_AI_LEADER_LL_TEKIN: It seems I've misjudged the stars and misjudged you. This is simply the cost.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DEFEAT_FROM_AI_LEADER_MER_MANN: I have fought many wars in my lifetime and the responsibility has weighed heavily on me and Finland. Brave Finns, you have fought your best but now it ends.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DEFEAT_FROM_HUMAN_LEADER_CVS_E: I may fall, but Switzerland has been occupied and freed in the past. Make no mistake, we will return and prosper once again.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DEFEAT_FROM_HUMAN_LEADER_CVS_I: Today you may have glory, but tomorrow you will come sooner than you think.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DEFEAT_FROM_HUMAN_LEADER_LEU_S: This is the exhaustion of death… I only regret not having anything else to sacrifice to the desire of contributing to the freedom of my country.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DEFEAT_FROM_HUMAN_LEADER_LIME_: A thousand curses upon you and your sons - may you never know peace as long as you reign, and may Resheph spill his fires upon you!
You didn't have to be my enemy; I only ever wanted to explore. In fact, in a way I envy you - now you make that journey to Adlivun, one that I've never had the chance for.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DEFEAT_FROM_HUMAN_LEADER_LL_TE: This outcome was clear to see. For anyone with eyes, that is.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DEFEAT_FROM_HUMAN_LEADER_MER_M: I saw that i had to uphold responsibility as commander, and defend the Finns from a tyranny such as yours.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DELEGATION_FROM_AI_LEADER_CVS_: The Swiss government has dispatched to you a delegation bringing gifts of cheese, chocolate, and some gold for your treasury. Please accept our hospitality.
I have sent a delegation with mangosteen, congee and the finest kuih dishes to express my gratitude for your kindness. I hope you enjoy them.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DELEGATION_FROM_AI_LEADER_GEDE: Ich sende Ihnen eine Wirtschaftsdelegation mit Geschenken aus meinem Land: Würstchen und Bier, viel Bier ...(I send you a business delegation with gifts from my country: sausages and beer, lots of beer ...)
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DELEGATION_FROM_AI_LEADER_JFD_: I send a delegation to you now, blessed as they are. May you accept them and the will of the Gods that follows.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DELEGATION_FROM_AI_LEADER_LEU_: I have sent a delegation to your Capital with some of the best meat you can find, chosen by the Gauchos themselves. Hope you enjoy!
I have sent my troops with some meat and books from Argentina, to feed our stomachs and our progress. Will you accept or are you just a barbarian?
I have dispatched a delegation bearing gifts of fine meats and cloth. The sturdy mules that bear these gifts are also yours should you want them.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DELEGATION_FROM_AI_LEADER_LIME: I've had some samples of our many riches delivered to you. How about some gold and rubies? A cup of wine, or two, or three?
I have sent scouts to your lands bearing gifts of whale meat and decorated hunting knives. Would you allow them to see your cities and tell their unipkaaqs?
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DELEGATION_FROM_AI_LEADER_LL_T: I have sent an ambassador to your city. House him as his prestige demands, but there is no need to give him servants - he is bringing his own.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DELEGATION_FROM_AI_LEADER_MER_: I have sent a delegation to your land with Karelian pasties and some of our finest literature. Enjoy them both.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DENOUNCE_FROM_AI_LEADER_CVS_ES: You are unworthy of my respect, or the respect of those around you, and I have ensured the world knows as much. (Denounces You)
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DENOUNCE_FROM_AI_LEADER_CVS_IS: A strong economy today is how we prepare for tomorrow. I see no future for your kingdom. (Denounces You)
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DENOUNCE_FROM_AI_LEADER_GEDEMO: Sie planen in unseren Rücken. Sei versichert, dass ich andere warnen werde! (You are plotting in our backs. Rest assured that I will warn others!) (Denounces You).
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DENOUNCE_FROM_AI_LEADER_JFD_OL: I have seen your future, and you are not one that can be dealt with through soft words (Denounces You).
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DENOUNCE_FROM_AI_LEADER_LEU_EV: I've got enough. I will echo my people in saying you are not to be trusted! (Denounces You).
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DENOUNCE_FROM_AI_LEADER_LEU_RO: You're so undeserving of the status of "Human Being", you and your people are no more than mere animals. (Denounces You).
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DENOUNCE_FROM_AI_LEADER_LEU_SA: The age of freedom and independence is coming and no longer shall the strong rule over the small with an iron fist. Change your ways or face the army of liberation (Denounces You).
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DENOUNCE_FROM_AI_LEADER_LIME_P: Never have I done business with one so awful as you - even your coins are tainted!
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DENOUNCE_FROM_AI_LEADER_LIME_T: If you do not see the world, how else can you protect our people?! How else can you approach destiny?!
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DENOUNCE_FROM_AI_LEADER_LL_TEK: It is plain for any to see your worthlessness and lack of respect. And yet I feel I must tell the world again. (Denounces You)
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DENOUNCE_FROM_AI_LEADER_MER_MA: How could anyone follow a leader such as yourself? Your people's loyalty is misguided, if they even have any loyalty towards you. (Denounces You).
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DENOUNCE_FROM_HUMAN_LEADER_CVS: Your words are empty and vapid. They shall not be forgotten, nor forgiven, by my people.
Words often fall on deaf ears when they are spoken by those who deserve no respect. Who are you again?
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DENOUNCE_FROM_HUMAN_LEADER_GED: Ich prangere dich öffentlich an! (I publicly denounce you.)
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DENOUNCE_FROM_HUMAN_LEADER_JFD: What shame you bring to yourself.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DENOUNCE_FROM_HUMAN_LEADER_LEU: You dare denounce me? I defeated emperors far mightier than you.
I do not fear the words of tyrants.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DENOUNCE_FROM_HUMAN_LEADER_LIM: Madness does always spring from the minds of the greedy.
You risk infuriating Sedna! Do you intend to drag us all down your path?
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DENOUNCE_FROM_HUMAN_LEADER_LL_: A poor gambit, and a poor-timed one. You have gained nothing.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DENOUNCE_FROM_HUMAN_LEADER_MER: I will make you pay for this. I swear by the Lord, you will pay!
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_DENOUNCE_REASON_FROM_AI_LEADER: (You are competing for the same City-States and are strong in Faith)
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_FIRST_MEET_LEADER_CVS_ESCHER_A: Ah, a traveller? Welcome, my friend, to this most beautiful nation we call Switzerland. I am Johan Heinrich Alfred Escher vom Glas - but please, just call me Alfred.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_FIRST_MEET_LEADER_CVS_ISKANDAR: Greetings traveller! I am Iskandar, first Sultan of Malacca. Tell me, what shores do you call your own?
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_FIRST_MEET_LEADER_GEDEMO_BISMA: Im Namen des großen deutschen Volkes heiße ich Euch willkommen! (In the name of the great German people, I bid you welcome!)
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_FIRST_MEET_LEADER_JFD_OLYMPIAS: In sight of great Mount Olympus, I greet you. I am Olympias, daughter of Neoptolemus.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_FIRST_MEET_LEADER_LEU_EVITA_AN: I'm pleased to meet you. My name is Eva Peron, but you may call me Evita. What brings you to Argentina?
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_FIRST_MEET_LEADER_LEU_ROCA_ANY: Well met. I'm Julio Argentino Roca. Yes, my second name is in fact Argentino, and I proudly live with it, and honour it and my nation with conquest and progress. And you are?
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_FIRST_MEET_LEADER_LEU_SANMARTI: Saludos! I am General José de San Martín, Liberator of Argentina and Protector of Peru. Long live the nation, freedom, and independence!
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_FIRST_MEET_LEADER_LIME_PHOE_AH: Greetings, and what will your pleasure be? Speak clearly - I shall have a scribe record this day!
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_FIRST_MEET_LEADER_LIME_THULE_D: Hail, fellow adventurer! I am Kiviuq, and my tribe is of the Thule people. Do you too have a wanderer's heart?
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_FIRST_MEET_LEADER_LL_TEKINICH_: A newcomer. Your arrival was not portended. I am the Lord of Oxhuitzá, and I am curious as to what you bring.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_FIRST_MEET_LEADER_MER_MANNERHE: Greetings from the Finns. We value loyalty above all else and do not fear military might, for who is more mighty than a man who loves his country?
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_FIRST_MEET_NEAR_INITIATOR_POSI: I am bestown with such kindness and grace.
I thank you for your kindness.
My merchants will be there at once.
I will join, with stargazers with clear eyes and warriors with strong arms.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_FIRST_MEET_NO_MANS_INFO_EXCHAN: I would like to propose that we share information on our nation's Capitals. It would certainly improve relations between our people, after all.
Let us exchange information on our capital cities and perhaps we can map out a prosperous trade route?
Ich lade Sie ein, Informationen über unsere jeweiligen Hauptstädte auszutauschen. (I invite you to exchange information on our respective capitals.)
I invite you to tell me about your Capital, and I would do the same.
Let's exchange some information of our capitals and learn more about our customs!
Let us exchange information on our capitals for the mutual growth of our people.
I suggest we exchange information on the locations of our capitals. I want to know more of your distant nation.
Come, see the majesty of Byblos! Remember to bring something to barter, for there are many merchants to meet!
Present yourself.
Life is full of chances to adventure. Would you make the journey to see my homelands?
You have not yet told me of your city. I wish to know what great monuments have been built in your name, and what stars you see.
We should exchange information.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_FIRST_MEET_VISIT_RECIPIENT_LEA: We are close to one of my cities, as it happens. Would you care to join me? Perhaps we can discuss new business ventures.
You must be tired from your travels. If you wish, you may visit our city nearby. Take a rest, enjoy the hospitality, and share with us stories of your culture. What do you say?
Hallo, ich bin Otto von Bismarck, Kanzler von Deutschland! Möchten Sie unsere nächste Stadt besuchen? (Hello, I am Otto von Bismarck, Chancellor of Germany! Would you like to visit our nearest city?)
We are close to my home. I offer my hospitality to you.
A Tango show is going to start at Caminito, do you mind joining us while we taste some nice Empanadas?
Just here there's an Estancia with some top-quality meat for us to enjoy, care to join us as civilized folk?
Would you care to visit one of Argentina's proud settlements? They abound with free and industrious citizens!
Would you be interested in a preliminary trade agreement? Perhaps you could come view a draft at a city of mine nearby.
Attend.
The season's ripe to hunt Bowhead, and I'm going on a hunting trip. Would you like to join?
A loyal vassal of mine is not far - we may use it to meet.
You should visit our beautiful lands, a land every Finn is proud to call home.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_GREETING_LEADER_CVS_ISKANDAR_H: It's good to see you again, friend. What can I do for you?
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_GREETING_LEADER_JFD_OLYMPIAS_A: Your return is welcome, if expected.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_GREETING_LEADER_LEU_ROCA_ANY: Your visit is welcome, as long as you don't come near my lands.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_KUDOS_LEADER_MER_MANNERHEIM_RE: (You share a government type and keep a large standing army)
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_KUDO_EXIT_LEADER_CVS_ESCHER_AN: A nation is nothing if it lacks productivity - and productivity cannot be accomplished without capital to build it. You understand this well.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_KUDO_EXIT_LEADER_CVS_ISKANDAR_: Your enthusiasm for the brightest minds this world has to offer is an example to the world.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_KUDO_EXIT_LEADER_JFD_OLYMPIAS_: You deal in the politics of mortals. It does not unseat me.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_KUDO_EXIT_LEADER_LEU_EVITA_ANY: You're truly an example. You keep your people happy and let your industry flourish!
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_KUDO_EXIT_LEADER_LEU_ROCA_ANY: You're an example to follow, truly you have progressed far.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_KUDO_EXIT_LEADER_LEU_SANMARTIN: May Heaven preside over your destinies and may you reach the summit of happiness and peace.
In these beatiful lands it is a great decision to train skilled horsemen.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_KUDO_EXIT_LEADER_LIME_PHOE_AHI: I never let good morals get in the way of good business. And by Astarte, we do have good business.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_KUDO_EXIT_LEADER_LIME_THULE_DA: Go far, and may your travels be eventful.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_KUDO_EXIT_LEADER_LL_TEKINICH_I: Your kingdom has clearly been blessed with ample harvest and good omens. It would be foolish to act against you.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_KUDO_EXIT_LEADER_MER_MANNERHEI: A nation is truly strong when each man sees himself as one who will defend his home and his faith unto death itself, against even death itself.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_KUDO_LEADER_CVS_ISKANDAR_REASO: (You have high population cities and many great people.)
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_KUDO_LEADER_GEDEMO_BISMARK_REA: (You have fought honorably and not capitulated in a peace deal.)
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_KUDO_LEADER_JFD_OLYMPIAS_REASO: (You are competing for the same City-States and are weak in Faith.)
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_KUDO_LEADER_LEU_EVITA_REASON_A: (You have High Production or Happy Citizens)
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_KUDO_LEADER_LEU_SANMARTIN_HORS: (You have a respectable amount of Horse Units)
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_KUDO_LEADER_LIME_PHOE_AHIRAM_B: (You're a warmonger, but at least you trade with him)
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_KUDO_LEADER_LL_TEKINICH_II_AGE: You have not infringed upon my vassals. It is more than I can say for others.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_KUDO_LEADER_LL_TEKINICH_II_REA: An empire as vast and strong as yours is clearly worthy of respect.
Rulers need to be careful, lest their plans be seen by you. If I had them, I would need to work hard to conceal them from you.
I respect your independence just as you respect mine.
Your name may not be as revered as mine, but trust that your place and your service is valued.
You may conduct your plans without my interference. I see that they have not interfered with mine.
Your priests know as much as mine, and for it your land prospers. Clearly, the gods favor you.
The stars shine bright on your empire. Your vassals must be very loyal.
The stars shine brightest in the dark. Prepare yourself. Our opportunity is nearly at hand.
The monuments of Oxhuitzá show it's great prestige. You have not attempted to make your name outshine mine.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MAKE_ALLIANCE_FROM_AI_LEADER_C: I am rarely in a position to call those around me 'allies', but you truly stand out as someone worthy of that title.
There are dangers in this world that will destroy us if we allow them. Let us form an alliance as a deterrent to those with opportunistic tendencies.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MAKE_ALLIANCE_FROM_AI_LEADER_G: Möchten Sie eine Allianz bilden? (Would you like to form an alliance?)
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MAKE_ALLIANCE_FROM_AI_LEADER_J: An alliance between you and I will bring glory to the Gods.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MAKE_ALLIANCE_FROM_AI_LEADER_L: Let us join forces for the shared good of our people
Let us form an alliance to destroy the uncivilized barbarians around us!
The soldiers of our land know no luxury but glory. Join with me, and we shall share this luxury with you and your own troops.
The time has come to expand our partnership! It has been quite profitable for me, at least.
You are not unlike an Agloolik. Would you be interested in going on an adventure?
We would be stronger together than apart. The stars and the politics are right for an alliance.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MAKE_ALLIANCE_FROM_AI_LEADER_M: You have shown great valor and wisdom in your leadership and i would ask we formalise our friendship and strengthen our nations.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MAKE_PEACE_AI_ACCEPT_DEAL_LEAD: I agree to this. Peace is much more profitable for both of us in the long term.
I agree, a peace treaty seems to be in both our interests.
Lass uns Frieden machen! (Let's make peace!)
The time has come then. I accept.
I will accept this peace.
Well fought...
My promises to the people for whom I have waged war have been fulfilled.
I believe that settles it, then.
Very well. Angakkuit shall ask Sedna to forgive us.
The Great Star demands blood. I am bound to accept nothing less.
I tire of this war, so i accept.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MAKE_PEACE_AI_REFUSE_DEAL_LEAD: With lives on the line, even a man without business sense could see this deal for what it is. Such a deal is unacceptable.
No, you will learn nothing should this war end now.
Natürlich nein. (Naturally no.)
The Gods guide me to triumph. I will not disappoint them with surrender.
I cannot accept your proposal.
There is no way my people will surrender!
No. I shall either be victorious, or I shall be nothing.
I am unwilling to pay such a ludicrous price for a worthless peace.
I am no fool, and the North Wind hasn't dulled my wits yet.
I cannot stand aside.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MAKE_PEACE_FROM_AI_LEADER_CVS_: I come to request that we lay down arms. I am sure we can both come to an agreement which would benefit us both.
The time has come to lay down arms. Let there be peace between us.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MAKE_PEACE_FROM_AI_LEADER_GEDE: Ich schlage einen Waffenstillstand vor, wann denkst du? (I propose a truce, when do you think?)
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MAKE_PEACE_FROM_AI_LEADER_JFD_: War has failed. We must find a way through peace.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MAKE_PEACE_FROM_AI_LEADER_LEU_: I believe it is time that we made peace.
I have taken enough from you, my troops need to rest sometimes... Shall we sign a treaty or something?
A well-fought defeat is worth more than a casual victory. Now is the time to lay down arms, don't you agree?
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MAKE_PEACE_FROM_AI_LEADER_LIME: Perhaps it is time we reconsidered our circumstances. Surely, there's something I could offer you?
Winter is coming, we should both be preparing for it. Can we agree to this truce?
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MAKE_PEACE_FROM_AI_LEADER_LL_T: The season of war is at its end. It is the proper time for a treaty.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MAKE_PEACE_FROM_AI_LEADER_MER_: I tire of this war, surely you must to?
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MODIFIER_AGENDA_JFD_ORACLE_CHT: Olmpias is pleased that you are no threat to her competition over City-States
Olympias feels threatened by your competition over City-States
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MODIFIER_CVS_ESCHER_HAPPY: Escher appreciates your economy and commends your productivity.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MODIFIER_CVS_ESCHER_UNHAPPY: Escher is displeased by your lack of productivity.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MODIFIER_CVS_ISKANDAR_HAPPY: Iskandar admires a populace filled with great people
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MODIFIER_CVS_ISKANDAR_UNHAPPY: Iskandar is disappointed in your weak economy
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MODIFIER_LEADER_LIME_PHOE_AHIR: Ahiram is happy to have an individual of your strengths on his payroll
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MODIFIER_LEADER_LIME_TEO_OWL_C: Spearthrower Owl hates those who interfere with City-States.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MODIFIER_LEADER_LIME_THULE_DAV: Kiviuq thinks you are close-minded and afraid of adventure
Kiviuq considers you a fellow explorer
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MODIFIER_LEADER_LL_TEKINICH_II: Te' K'inich II regards your empire as unpopulous, and therefore weak
Te' K'inich II sees your empire as large enough to deserve respect
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MODIFIER_LEU_EVITA_FOE: Eva Peron doesn't like your current government
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MODIFIER_LEU_EVITA_FRIEND: Eva Peron is pleased you keep your citizens happy and productive-
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MODIFIER_LEU_ROCA_BORDERS: Roca dislikes civilizations that settle or have units close to his borders
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MODIFIER_LEU_ROCA_TECH: Roca doesn't respect civilizations with less technologies than him
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MODIFIER_LEU_SANMARTIN_CITIES: San Martin dislikes the amount of cities you captured
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MODIFIER_LEU_SANMARTIN_HORSES: San Martin respects you for your dedication to mounted units
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_MODIFIER_MER_MANNERHEIM_MARSHA: Mannerheim is concerned by your government and standing army.
Mannerheim is happy you share his government type and keep a large standing army
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_OPEN_BORDERS_FROM_AI_LEADER_CV: Opening our borders is a great show of trust and friendship, and today I must request such a commitment from you; would you care to grant me this?
What will become of trade if we cannot travel with free passage? I humbly request that you open your borders. What say you?
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_OPEN_BORDERS_FROM_AI_LEADER_GE: Sind Sie damit einverstanden, dass wir Ihr Territorium durchqueren? (Will you allow our units to cross through your territory?)
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_OPEN_BORDERS_FROM_AI_LEADER_JF: I invite you to join me in an open borders agreement.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_OPEN_BORDERS_FROM_AI_LEADER_LE: Let's tand united and share our territories!
Don't make me regret this offer.
The Revolution against tyranny must continue! Would you allow my troops to pass through your lands so that we may achieve this goal?
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_OPEN_BORDERS_FROM_AI_LEADER_LI: I have a proposal that I believe will generate opportunities between us?
I've heard many legends from your realm. Could I travel there and see if they're true?
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_OPEN_BORDERS_FROM_AI_LEADER_LL: I ask for free movement through your borders. It would aid in eliminating threats, and I will make the necessary offerings.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_OPEN_BORDERS_FROM_AI_LEADER_ME: I hope you can accept these terms.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_REJECT_DECLARE_FRIEND_FROM_AI_: No, it would only bring misfortune.
This is most unnerving. But no matter, my people love me without your approval.
It is foolish to go alone - Amaruq hunts lone travellers. I can overcome him, but I fear for your sake.
You will be left weaker by your choice.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_REJECT_DECLARE_FRIEND_FROM_HUM: It is with a heavy heart that I must reject your offer at this time, but please feel free to ask again at a later date.
I see no friend in you.
Ich weigere mich, der Welt unsere Freundschaft zu erklären. (I refuse such a ridiculous offer.)
I won't have it.
I'm afraid I can't accept your proposal.
I'm afraid I can't accept your proposal.
No. I only want those who are Lions as friends.
This does not seem a... mutually beneficial venture.
I'm afraid that my path goes elsewhere.
The Great Star is out of alignment. Any friendship sworn this day would be ill-fated.
Let us keep our relations purely formal in nature.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_REJECT_DELEGATION_FROM_HUMAN_L: Ah, I'm afraid I cannot agree to this for now.
I'm sorry, but I cannot allow that at this time.
Nein, leider. (Unfortunately, no.)
Misfortune follows you delegation. I cannot accept.
I'm afraid that I can't accept, I must respect my people's wishes
No.
I cannot accept these offerings.
Your delegation will not be allowed, but perhaps I could interest you in some trinkets? For affordable costs?
I fear it's tirigusuusiit. I should not agree.
We have not yet built the household suitable for your delegate. Perhaps later.
I cannot accept.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_REJECT_MAKE_DEAL_FROM_AI_LEADE: A pity that we could not come to an arrangement.
I'd appreciate a better deal than this.
Do you presume me to be a fool?
No, it would only bring misfortune.
This is most unnerving. But no matter, my people love me without your approval.
I believe we shall need to do some revising.
It is foolish to go alone - Amaruq hunts lone travellers. I can overcome him, but I fear for your sake.
You will be left weaker by your choice.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_REJECT_OPEN_BORDERS_FROM_HUMAN: I apologise, but I lack the inclination to accept this deal at present.
I'm sorry, but I cannot allow that at this time.
Wir sind im Moment nicht interessiert. (We are not interested at the moment.)
I cannot accept such things.
I have no interest on this arrangement, for now.
These lands are beautiful, not for uncivilized folk such as you.
Argentina's doors are closed to tyrants.
No, I don't think we shall.
Ah, can't you explore somewhere else?
I have not received the customary offerings. The border will remain shut.
I cannot accept these terms, not in good mind.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_WARNING_DONT_SETTLE_NEAR_ME_AI: It would seem that I have a new neighbor. However, I feel borders may become blurred should we continue to encroach on each other's territory. Please do not let this happen again.
I have noticed you that you settled in Malaccan territory. Wars have been started over less. Let this be a warning.
Don't be silly, friend. There is enough room for the both of us.
I shall settle cities where I please. If you have a problem with that, I'll meet your army at the gates.
My sincere apologies, we didn't mean to intrude. We shall look elsewhere next time.
I didn't realise you were the apparent owner of this land. Very well, but you may want mark out your territory next time.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_WARNING_EXIT_LEADER_CVS_ESCHER: For all you can or have done, your people do little and your treasury is nearly empty. You set a poor example for those around you.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_WARNING_EXIT_LEADER_CVS_ISKAND: Doomed is the nation that ignores its economy. Do you not care for the prosperity of your people?
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_WARNING_EXIT_LEADER_GEDEMO_BIS: Du bist ein Weichei! (You are a wimp!).
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_WARNING_EXIT_LEADER_JFD_OLYMPI: Your favour with the Gods is short-lived.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_WARNING_EXIT_LEADER_LEU_EVITA_: Your people riot and don't produce anything. I'm afraid I agree with them, as your vile government only has them oppressed.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_WARNING_EXIT_LEADER_LEU_ROCA_A: I warn you, I kill any uncivilized barbarian that threatens my rightful lands!
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_WARNING_EXIT_LEADER_LEU_SANMAR: The real contest in the world is between those who value freedom and those who do not, and you… you are on the wrong side.
I see you believe these lands are yours. These lands are of the Gauchos and we shall fight for it.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_WARNING_EXIT_LEADER_LIME_PHOE_: War is not good for profits. Unless, of course, it is against the warmongers.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_WARNING_EXIT_LEADER_LIME_THULE: You are no traveller. Only an obstacle, that I will overcome.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_WARNING_EXIT_LEADER_LL_TEKINIC: My priests wonder why Oxhuitzá should acknowledge your whims. I see no reason for it.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_WARNING_EXIT_LEADER_MER_MANNER: Fortifications, artillery, foreign aid -- how will these be of value, unless the ordinary soldier knows that it is HE guarding his country?
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_WARNING_LEADER_GEDEMO_BISMARK_: (You have never gone to war or have capitulated in a peace deal.)
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_WARNING_LEADER_JFD_OLYMPIAS_RE: (You are competing for the same City-States and are strong in Faith.)
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_WARNING_LEADER_LEU_ROCA_REASON: (You have less technologies discovered than him)
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_WARNING_LEADER_LL_TEKINICH_II_: Oxhuitzá is an overlord city, and it requires underlings. Prove your strength, lest you become one.
Your blindness is legendary. You would not know you've been betrayed until your heart has already been torn from you chest.
Your conquests reveal your schemes. They show an insecure, petty overlord unworthy of respect.
The gods demand offerings, and my priests have suggested your head. I agree with them.
I will accept no overlord. Do not presume yourself mine.
Do not attempt to surpass me. Oxhuitzá shall not be denied!
Those city-states must serve the better overlord. It is plain to see who that is.
Your servants pray for a worthier master. An overlord like Oxhuitzá would be welcomed by them.
Your arrogance is only rivaled by Tikal's, and you are destined for the same fate.
Your stupidity and backwardness does not offend me. On the contrary, you have gifted me an opportunity!
Oxhuitzá is clearly favored. Your paltry efforts merely make it look greater by comparison.
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_WARNING_LEADER_MER_MANNERHEIM_: (You have a different government type and keep a large standing army)
en_US.LOC_DIPLO_WARNING_TOO_MANY_TROOPS_NEAR_M: In defending the interests of the weak and persecuted anywhere in this world, I needn't achknowledge political borders. Your tyranny must end.
I do apologise for startling you. I can assure you that this was a routine military exercise, not an act of aggression.
Very well. This will not be forgotten.
I certainly hope that you are not planning on invading my nation. Please, move your troops from my borders before you make a terrible mistake.
I say this with good will; please remove your troops from my borders or it will be seen as an act of aggression.
My my, what a magnificent display of force. Of course, if it is war you are looking for, know that our power extends beyond the ports of Malacca.

Ein übelster Haufen von Soldaten, die sich in der Nähe unserer Grenzen gebildet haben ... Willst du sie entfernen, bevor ein unglücklicher Vorfall eintritt? (A nauseabond pile of soldiers formed near our borders ... do you want to remove them before an unfortunate incident occurs?)
Come then. I am prepared to fight you. I have a son born of Zeus. What do you have?
Know that I will protect Argentina from any outside treat. So please I ask you to move your troops.
My troops are ready to destroy your troops near my borders. Leave.
Your troops gather near our borders. I warn you: If you intend on war, even the rocks of Argentina will rise to reject foreign invaders.
I have read reports of forces amassing near my border, bearing your flag. Do you have anything to say? Perhaps a plea for mercy?
I see you.
Those do not look like adventurers on my border. Or hunters. In fact, they appear to be invaders. My eyes aren't stone yet.
Your schemes are as foolish as they are transparent. You have no advantage. Turn back.
Brave Finns stand ready to repel any attack, you'd be wise to remember that.

en_US.LOC_DISTRICT_LEU_ARRABAL_DESCRIPTION: Argentine unique replacement for the Neighborhood district. Aside from the base housing based on appeal, Arrabales also generate +1 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production for every 2 adjacent districts. When adjacent to a district it also generates +1 [ICON_GREATPERSON] Great Musician Point.
en_US.LOC_DISTRICT_LEU_ESTANCIA_DESCRIPTION: Replacement for the Encampment district for Roca's Argentina, unlocked with Horseback Riding. Estancias allow Military Engineers to be trained without Armories and 25% Faster, and increase the Border Expansion rate by 25%. They also have a [ICON_FOOD] Food Adjacency Bonus with Pastures and Forts.

en_US.LOC_ERA_ANCIENT_DESCRIPTION: From the first stirrings of life beneath water… to the great beasts of the Stone Age… to man taking his first upright steps, you have come far.  Now begins your greatest quest: from this early cradle of civilization on towards the stars.
en_US.LOC_ERA_ATOMIC_DESCRIPTION: New frontiers of discovery expand our understanding, from the tiny atom to the majesty of outer space. Mysteries long tolerated are closer than ever to revealing their deepest secrets, beyond what we can easily see. You will choose how to use this knowledge, and push back the greatest darkness we have yet faced.
en_US.LOC_ERA_CLASSICAL_DESCRIPTION: From humble beginnings, you have shown remarkable growth. Leave your bronze for iron and rule with horse and sword. The sky above begins to reveal its secrets, a collection of heaven that uplifts our hearts and guides us to foreign shores.
en_US.LOC_ERA_INDUSTRIAL_DESCRIPTION: The steady hum of machinery, the acrid smell of smoke, vision clouded by ash and soot – these are the signs of changing times. The lure of scientific and cultural advancement is the engine driving your realm forward.  Now your challenge is to maintain the delicate balance between earth and man, between peace and war.
en_US.LOC_ERA_INFORMATION_DESCRIPTION: A world of information rests in the palm of your hand, and networks for instantaneous communication span the globe.  Yet a unified vision of our future has never been built.  We compete in technology, culture, and politics. We have deadly weapons that could destroy our planet. Lead us carefully, but boldly, and build a global community that can stand for years to come.
en_US.LOC_ERA_MEDIEVAL_DESCRIPTION: You have built great cities of stone and seen early empires rise and fall.  Soon you will stand under the towering pinnacles of castles alongside your gallant knights. That is where the story of your people will be written. Just as the young apprentice learns to carry a sword, so shall you grow to understand your place in this world.
en_US.LOC_ERA_MODERN_DESCRIPTION: In the beginning, legends of flying men soared. And today, you are on the brink of transforming those legends into a reality. With flight and new forms of communication you can create a small and intimate world.  But at what cost? Our competing ideas of how to govern and how to live threaten to bring conflict on a global scale.  You must choose your own path through this rising din of ideological oratory.
en_US.LOC_ERA_RENAISSANCE_DESCRIPTION: New powers call forth, from the barrel of muskets to flowers of fire in the sky. Even the quiet words on newly printed pages hold great changes within. The world, once so vast and mysterious, has grown smaller and more familiar. Yet, there are always questions to be answered, faiths to be tested, and national identities to be formed.
