en_US.LOC_FEATURE_BARRINGER_CRATER_DESCRIPTION: One tile natural wonder. Provides +5 [ICON_SCIENCE] Science, +2 [ICON_FOOD] Food and +3 [ICON_GOLD] Gold. +15% [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production toward Space Race Projects if you own this tile.
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_BARRINGER_CRATER_QUOTE: "In fact we can now prove that this crater is due to the collision with the earth of an extra-terrestrial body, possibly a small asteroid, which was presumably metallic in nature."[NEWLINE]- Daniel Barringer
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_BIOLUMINESCENT_BAY_DESCRIPTI: One tile natural wonder. Appears as a Reef and provides +5 [ICON_SCIENCE] Science, +1 [ICON_FOOD] Food, and +1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold. +1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold on Fishing Boats if you own this tile.
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_BIOLUMINESCENT_BAY_QUOTE: "The emission of light from fire, lightning bolts, stars or living beings attracts the attention of any human being. In the case of bioluminescence the light has a strange glow, something magic and mysterious."[NEWLINE]- Cassius Stevani'
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_CERRO_DE_POTOSI_DESCRIPTION: One tile impassable natural wonder. Appears as a Mountain and provides +1 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and +3 [ICON_GOLD] Gold to adjacent tiles.
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_CERRO_DE_POTOSI_QUOTE: "I am rich Potosi, treasure of the world, king of all mountains and envy of kings."[NEWLINE]- First Coat of Arms of Potosi
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_DALLOL_DESCRIPTION: One tile natural wonder. Provides +2 [ICON_SCIENCE] Science, +2 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production, +2 [ICON_FOOD] Food and +1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold.
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_DALLOL_QUOTE: "There is hell, there is darkness, there is the sulfurous pit — burning, scalding, stench, consumption!"[NEWLINE]- William Shakespeare, King Lear
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_GIBRALTAR_DESCRIPTION: One tile impassable natural wonder. Provides +1 [ICON_FOOD] Food and +1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold to adjacent tiles.
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_GIBRALTAR_QUOTE: "Look round, my boys, and view how beautiful the Rock appears by the light of the glorious fire."[NEWLINE]- George Augustus Eliott
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_GRAND_MESA_DESCRIPTION: One tile impassable natural wonder. Provides +1 [ICON_FOOD] Food and +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture to adjacent tiles.
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_GRAND_MESA_QUOTE: "Conservation means the wise use of the earth and its resources for the lasting good of men."[NEWLINE]- Gifford Pinchot'
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_KAILASH_DESCRIPTION: One tile impassable natural wonder. Appears as a Mountain and provides +1 [ICON_Faith] Faith and +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture to adjacent tiles. +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture from foreign Cities following your [ICON_RELIGION] Religion if you own this tile.
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_KAILASH_QUOTE: "After thus having instructed the godly ones Lord Brahma went away with in his wake the forefathers and the leaders of the people whom he took from his own place to the abode of Lord Shiva, Kailash, the best of all mountains that is so dear to the master."[NEWLINE]- The Bhagavata Purana
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_KRAKATOA_DESCRIPTION: One tile impassable natural wonder. Appears as a Volcano and provides +2 [ICON_SCIENCE] Science to adjacent tiles. Provides additional yields on eruption at the cost of [ICON_Citizen] Population and damage to infrastructure. Always active.
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_KRAKATOA_QUOTE: "I saw with amazement that the island of Krakatoa lay completely burnt and barren in front of our eyes and that at four locations was throwing up large chunks of fire."[NEWLINE]- Johann Wilhelm Vogel
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_LAKE_VICTORIA_DESCRIPTION: Four tile natural wonder. Appears as a Lake and provides +2 [ICON_FOOD] Food, +2 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production, +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold.
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_LAKE_VICTORIA_QUOTE: "I saw that old father Nile without any doubt rises in the Victoria Nyanza, and as I had foretold, that lake is the great source of the holy river which cradled the first expounder of our religious belief."[NEWLINE]- John Hanning Speke
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_LENCOIS_MARANHENSES_DESCRIPT: Two tile natural wonder. Provides +2 [ICON_FOOD] Food, +2 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +2 [ICON_GOLD]. +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture on Desert and Plains Floodplains if you own at least one of these tiles. Provides fresh water.
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_LENCOIS_MARANHENSES_QUOTE: "I saw meadows of white and golden sands, ever shifting their shape according to the creative mood and whim of the winds."[NEWLINE]- Geert Mauricio Bas
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_MOSI_OA_TUNYA_DESCRIPTION: One tile impassable natural wonder. Provides +2 [ICON_FOOD] Food to adjacent tiles. Provides +4 Appeal to adjacent tiles isntead of the usual +2. Provides fresh water.
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_MOSI_OA_TUNYA_QUOTE: "Creeping with awe to the verge, I peered down into a large rent and saw that a stream of a thousand yards broad leaped down a hundred feet, and then became suddenly compressed into a space of fifteen or twenty yards, the most wonderful sight I had witnessed in Africa."[NEWLINE]- David Livingstone
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_MOTLATSE_CANYON_DESCRIPTION: Four tile impassable natural wonder. Provides +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture and +1 [ICON_FAITH] Faith to adjacent tiles.
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_MOTLATSE_CANYON_QUOTE: "I believe that South Africa is the most beautiful place on earth. Admittedly, I am biased, but I think even the most scrupulous critic would agree that we have been blessed with a truly wonderful land."[NEWLINE]- Nelson Mandela
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_NAMIB_DESCRIPTION: Three tile natural wonder. Provides +2 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture, +2 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and +2 [ICON_GOLD] Gold. Recon units that enter Namib Sand Sea tiles receive the ability 'Desert Nomads' (+1 [ICON_Movement] Movement).
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_NAMIB_QUOTE: "I love to hear the sound made by sand dunes, I am one of those who perceive the rhythm of a landscape as recorded in many paintings, I am one of thousands who know I am finally home."[NEWLINE]- Mvula Ya Nangolo
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_OLD_FAITHFUL_DESCRIPTION: One tile natural wonder. Provides +3 [ICON_SCIENCE] Science, +2 [ICON_FOOD] Food, +1 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production, +1 [ICON_Faith] Faith, and +1 [ICON_GOLD] Gold. Major adjacency bonus to Campus, Seowon and Observatory districts.
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_OLD_FAITHFUL_QUOTE: "It spouted at regular intervals nine times during our stay, the columns of boiling water being thrown from ninety to one hundred and twenty-five feet at each discharge, which lasted from fifteen to twenty minutes. We gave it the name of Old Faithful."[NEWLINE]- Nathaniel P. Langford
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_OUNIANGA_DESCRIPTION: Two tile natural wonder. Provides +2 [ICON_FOOD] Food, +2 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture, and +2 [ICON_GOLD] Gold. Provides +1 [ICON_FOOD] Food to adjacent tiles. Provides fresh water.
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_OUNIANGA_QUOTE: "At the beginning, the language of the desert was grass blooming against the wall of wind, tall palms swaying in the season of seeding and cinders carried by air to the blue welcome of warm sand. She was our first fountain, our mother, who held us, then gave us away to the age of waiting cities."[NEWLINE]- Al-Munsif al-Wahaybi
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_SALAR_DE_UYUNI_DESCRIPTION: Four tile natural wonder. Provides +2 [ICON_SCIENCE] Science, +2 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and +4 [ICON_GOLD] Gold. If you own at least one Salar de Uyuni tile, Mines on resources in your empire provide +2 [ICON_GOLD] Gold.
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_SALAR_DE_UYUNI_QUOTE: "I shivered in those solitudes when I heard the voice of the salt in the desert."[NEWLINE]- Pablo Neruda
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_SINAI_DESCRIPTION: One tile impassable natural wonder. Appears as a Mountain and provides +3 [ICON_Faith] Faith to adjacent tiles. Religious units that move next to Mount Sinai receive the ability 'Ten Commandments' (+15 [ICON_RELIGION] Religious Strength).
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_SINAI_QUOTE: "When the Lord finished speaking to Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two tablets of the covenant law, the tablets of stone inscribed by the finger of God."[NEWLINE]- Exodus 31:18
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_SRI_PADA_DESCRIPTION: One tile impassable natural wonder. Appears as a Mountain and provides +1 [ICON_FOOD] Food and +1 [ICON_Faith] Faith to adjacent tiles.
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_SRI_PADA_QUOTE: "An exceedingly wondrous sight, which is endowed with supreme splendour."[NEWLINE]- The Mahabharata
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_VREDEFORT_DOME_DESCRIPTION: Two tile natural wonder. Provides +2 [ICON_FOOD] Food, +1 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production, +2 [ICON_SCIENCE] Science, and +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture.
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_VREDEFORT_DOME_QUOTE: "When geologists first wandered the spectacular ring of hills straddling the Vaal River north of Vredefort nearly 150 years ago, they immediately recognised that the unusually shattered and uptilted rocks bore witness to an exceptionally violent event in the distant past."[NEWLINE]- Wolf Uwe Reimold
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_WULINGYUAN_DESCRIPTION: Two tile impassable natural wonder. Provides +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture to adjacent tiles.
en_US.LOC_FEATURE_WULINGYUAN_QUOTE: "From ten thousand valleys the trees touch heaven, on a thousand peaks cuckoos are calling, and, after a night of mountain rain, from each summit come hundreds of silken cascades."[NEWLINE]- Wang Wei

en_US.LOC_GAMEMODE_ANONYMOUS_DESCRIPTION: Players are all anonymous![NEWLINE]No more side-arrangement.
en_US.LOC_GAMEMODE_LASTMOVE_DESCRIPTION: Infamous end of turn last move first move are coming to an end![NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Moving or attacking during the last 15 secs of the turn would make your unit [COLOR_Civ6Red]Unprepared[ENDCOLOR].[NEWLINE][COLOR_Civ6Red]Unprepared[ENDCOLOR] units have a -20[ICON_Strength] penalty when attacking.[NEWLINE]An unit will stays [COLOR_Civ6Red]Unprepared[ENDCOLOR] until it is attacked or after 10 secs in the following game turn.
en_US.LOC_GAMEMODE_SUDDEN_DEATH_DESCRIPTION: Players are gradually eliminated based on their score as the clock is inexorably ticking...Standing the test of time has just taken a whole new meaning!

en_US.LOC_GOVERNOR_LIME_TEO_OWL_EMISSARY_DESC: The Spearthrower Owl requires vassal City-states to be kept in line, and for this task Fire Is Born is perfect. Through a mix of conquest, spycraft, diplomacy, and exploitation, he is able to enforce his benefactor's demands swiftly, ably, and permanently. Those wayward vassals will never leave the empire again.
en_US.LOC_GOVERNOR_PROMOTION_AGRICULTURE_DESCR: +1 [ICON_FOOD] Food on the city's revealed resources.
en_US.LOC_GOVERNOR_PROMOTION_AMBASSADOR_NEGOTI: City cannot be put under siege and gains +5 City Defense Strength.
en_US.LOC_GOVERNOR_PROMOTION_EDUCATOR_EUREKA_D: Campus buildings in this city provide additional Science. +3 [ICON_SCIENCE] Science for Library, +5 [ICON_SCIENCE] Science for University, +7 [ICON_SCIENCE] Science for Research Lab.
en_US.LOC_GOVERNOR_PROMOTION_EDUCATOR_KNOWLEDG: Domestic [ICON_TRADEROUTE] Trade Routes to Pingala's city provide +1 [ICON_FOOD] Food and +3 [ICON_SCIENCE] Science.
en_US.LOC_GOVERNOR_PROMOTION_MERCHANT_INVESTOR: +1 [ICON_SCIENCE] Science and +1 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture for foreign traders going through this city. Increasing to +2 [ICON_SCIENCE] Science and +2 [ICON_CULTURE] Culture with Economics.
en_US.LOC_GOV_PROMO_LIME_TEO_OWL_EMISSARY_ARRI: May be assigned to a City-State, where it provides 1 [ICON_ENVOY] envoy. Friendly units inside this City-State borders gain +5 [ICON_STRENGTH] Combat strength.
en_US.LOC_GOV_PROMO_LIME_TEO_OWL_EMISSARY_EXPE: [ICON_STRENGTH] Combat Strength +10 for this City-state's garrison.
en_US.LOC_GOV_PROMO_LIME_TEO_OWL_EMISSARY_FALL: [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production +25% for Commercial Hub and City Center buildings in your cities within a 15-tile radius.
en_US.LOC_GOV_PROMO_LIME_TEO_OWL_EMISSARY_OUTP: If you're sending a [ICON_TRADEROUTE] traderoute to this City-State, [ICON_ENVOY] envoys sent count as two.[NEWLINE][ICON_PRODUCTION] Production +25% for Commercial Hub in your cities within a 15-tile radius.
en_US.LOC_GOV_PROMO_LIME_TEO_OWL_EMISSARY_OVER: Levied units within 10 tiles of this City-state receive +5 [ICON_STRENGTH] Combat Strength.
en_US.LOC_HAGIA_SOPHIA_MOVEMENT_ABILITY: +2 [ICON_MOVEMENT] Movement for Missionaries, Apostles and Gurus (Hagia Sophia).
en_US.LOC_HOLY_SITE_HARBOR_ADJACENCY_DESCRIPTI: +{1_num} [ICON_GOLD] Gold from the adjacent Holy Site.
en_US.LOC_IMPROVEMENT_LIME_THULE_WBH_DESCRIPTI: Unique improvement for Thule, unlocked at Sailing.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][ICON_FOOD] Food +1 if built on a Tundra tile (doubled on snow), [ICON_CULTURE] Culture +1 and [ICON_FAITH] Faith +1 for each adjacent sea resource and Camp tile.[NEWLINE]Must be built adjacent to a resource tile. Can be placed on forests.
en_US.LOC_IMPROVEMENT_MER_SAUNA_DESCRIPTION: Finnish unique improvement. +1 Appeal and +0.5 [ICON_Housing] Housing. +1 [ICON_Culture] Culture and +1 [ICON_Production] Production. Additional +1 [ICON_Culture] Culture for every 2 adjacent Woods and +1 [ICON_Production] Production from adjacent Camps. +1 [ICON_Amenities] Amenity when adjacent to a river. Can be built on Grass, Plains, Tundra, Snow, Woods or Marsh, but not adjacent to another Sauna. Provides [ICON_Tourism] Tourism equal to the tile's Appeal after Flight.
en_US.LOC_INVALID_SLOT_HUMAN_REQUIRED_TT: This player slot needs occupied by a human player to start the game.
en_US.LOC_INVALID_SLOT_MAP_SIZE_TT: This player slot is unavailable for the current map size. Have the host increase the map size or swap to an available player slot.
en_US.LOC_INVITE_BUTTON_TT: Invite friends from your Steam friends list to this game.
en_US.LOC_JOIN_CODE_POPUP_TEXT: Join a game by using a Join Code. The Join Code can be found in the Game Summary tab of the game's Staging Room. Join Codes are case sensitive.
en_US.LOC_KICK_VOTE_TT: Kick Voting requires a majority vote to successfully kick a player from the game.
en_US.LOC_KNOWN_GRAPHICS_CARD_ISSUES: There are known issues that may occur when running the DirectX 12 version of Civilization VI with your current hardware configuration. The DirectX 12 version currently requires a compatible graphics card, either AMD or NVidia (Maxwell series or later).

en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_BARBAROSSA: Heroic Frederick, king of the Germans, your task is to forge the independent states that surround you into an empire. You are blessed to be a great military leader – use those skills to bring these cities under your sway so they may develop into commercial and industrial powerhouses.  Surely then the bards will sing of mighty Frederick with the red beard, the great Holy Roman Emperor.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_CATHERINE_DE_MED: It falls to you, Catherine de Medici, to use your gifts of knowledge and of the arts to unite your people. Steer carefully through these troubled times, Queen Mother of France. You will build great wonders, drawing visitors from all corners of the earth. With your keen awareness of all things, both those seen and those hidden in the shadows, your empire will certainly stand the test of time.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_CLEOPATRA: There will be those who underestimate you, but you are cunning and full of tricks, Queen Cleopatra. Your charm will establish indestructible alliances with the strongest leaders of the world. Keep your friends close by your side and you will find yourself untouchable, with the glory of Egypt primed to win over the world.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_CVS_ESCHER: Trust in your ambition, Alfred Escher, great pioneer of railways, for the cantons of Switzerland call upon your leadership. Within your humble nation, you will plan wisely, using the mountainous landscape to transform industry. Remain true to your council, show kindness to smaller nations, and in turn your cantons shall find reward.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_CVS_ISKANDAR: The merchants of Malacca await your call, legendary Iskandar, usurped shah of Temasek. Cultivate relationships with the City-States that surround you, and in time the greatest merchants, scholars and artisans shall surely flock to the golden peninsula. Set a precedent in controlling maritime trade, expand Malacca's power and influence, and she will write a legend of her own.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_DEFAULT: It is up to you to lead your people to glory by building a civilization that will stand the test of time.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_GANDHI: Be kind, Gandhi Bapu, and you will find yourself surrounded by true friends. Keep the Indian people safe, guarding them with magnificent elephant warriors. Your faith will guide you to peace and harmony. Keep your mind open, and be the change you want to see in the world.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_GEDEMO_BISMARK: Hail mighty Bismarck, first chancellor of Germany and her empire! Germany is an upstart nation, fashioned from the ruins of the Holy Roman Empire and finally unified in 1871, a little more than a century ago. The German people have proven themselves to be creative, industrious and ferocious warriors. Despite enduring great catastrophe in the first half of the 20th century, Germany remains a worldwide economic, artistic and technological leader. Great Prince Bismarck, the German people look to you to lead them to greater days of glory. Their determination is strong and they turn to you, their beloved iron chancellor, to guide them once more. Will you rule and conquer through blood and iron, or foster the Germanic arts and industry? Can you build a civilization that will stand the test of time?
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_GILGAMESH: Much rests upon your shoulders, King Gilgamesh. Your own people, and many people of the world, look to you as leader. But you are more than a mere man, and the weight of the world will never cause you to waver. Encourage the people of Sumer to settle the fertile lands along rivers, and be sure to choose your allies carefully - for there will be many vying for a piece of your strength. Venture forth, for it is time to begin your epic tale.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_GORGO: Gorgo, Queen of Sparta; glory to you and your loyal hoplite armies! Greece savors the blessings from Ares that every victory brings. And your people applaud your thoughtful governance and cultural marvels. Stand proud, for the legacy of Greece, and of your achievements, will be told over and over again for generations.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_HARDRADA: All men fear the approach of your ships, King Harald of Norway, Thunderbolt of the North. Your longboats dominate the waves, always at the ready to unleash their berserker armies on an unsuspecting shore.  May Odin bless your kingdom and may the skalds sing tales of the victories of your mighty warriors.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_HOJO: The great wave of Buddhism follows you, Shikken of Japan, Hojo Tokimune. Your people truly understand what it is to practice balance, and even your finest samurai will be well-learned and spiritually apt. Be strong, embrace the divine wind, and you will reach enlightenment.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_JFD_OLYMPIAS: You have dreamed of a vision, Queen Olympias - of a thunderbolt fallen upon your womb and of the fires of Zeus spreading through your body. You have been blessed. A son will be born to take the throne of the world and all with it. And you must be his herald.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_LEU_EVITA: The proud people of Argentina look up to you, Eva Peron. Hear the problems of your citizens, and give more rights to those that need it. With the work of the Descamisados build your nation to become an example of both cultural improvements and local production. Call forth the Gauchos and let them feed your people, while they compose beautiful Tango music on your Arrabales. Let your people rejoice again as they are led by the one they happily called: Evita.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_LEU_ROCA: The proud people of Argentina look up to you, Julio Roca, president and great lieutenant. Lead your nation to glory by defeating the enemies that dare stand in your borders, as you expand the land and might of Argentina. Make use of the colonial Estancias to feed and empower your people, as well as strategic points in your conquests. You are called to bring Argentina to a new age of glory above your neighbors. Should you succeed, great Julio Argentino Roca, your people will forever remember you.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_LEU_SANMARTIN: A continent rises up alongside you, José de San Martín, esteemed general and protector of liberty. Your Army of the Andes is a mighty force for freedom and the strength of your loyal Granaderos is unparalleled. Go now, Libertador, and break the chains of foreign domination that bind the peoples of this continent. Let there be freedom, the rest matters not!
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_LIME_PHOE_AHIRAM: Melqart grants you prosperity, Ahiram, as few are as wealthy as you. Use your dominance over the seas in order to bolster your own wealth, but do not simply hoard it. Order lavish constructions across all your holdings, and inspire merchantry and business to thrive in your colonies, for riches beget riches. In a world of beggars, use the gold and silver of Byblos and beyond to build great cities - and yes, a civilization - that will stand the test of time.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_LIME_TEO_OWL: Teotihuacan hungers. Your armies stand ready to bend the world to your will. Let fire consume all defiant, upstart kings so that you may take what Teotihuacan requires - wealth, power, blood. Cast your divine shadow across the world. Let nobody stand outside it.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_LIME_THULE_DAVE: A vast expanse lies before you, heroic Kiviuq, eternal wanderer. Your people are a pious and cultured one, with relics beyond comparison and legends beyond belief. Send your hunters out to hunt for whales, and let your Angakkuit duel with Sedna so that you may have good fortune. But do not forget to explore, and lead your scouts out to the ends of the horizon. Fight hard and overcome odds, and above all do not let your heart turn to stone.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_LL_TEKINICH_II: The stars are right, Te' K'inich II, perfect for your rule. Take advantage of opportunities as they arise, and strike down rival city-states at the opportune moment. Claim the spoils of war from your conquests, so that your kingdom may grow stronger and vaster. Watch as the gods themselves reward you for bringing your kingdom to its apex! Revel in the glory of the gods, Yajaw, for your time is at hand.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_MER_MANNERHEIM: And so we look to you again, Carl Mannerheim, to lead the Finnish people in brave defense of our homelands. Bolster the loyalty of your citizens and outwit the schemes of your enemies with superior military intelligence. Your tenacity will remind both friend and foe how great our love for Finland's many beauties and pleasures is, and the length to which we will protect her!
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_MVEMBA: Mother Earth has many gifts for you, King Mvemba a Nzinga. Your people know the dense woods and rainforests as their homes, and glide through them with ease.  Great also are the gifts that come from travelers of distant lands. Keep an open mind, for the inspiration of the open world will let our people create art with power and majesty.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_PEDRO: Your people look to you, Emperor Pedro II, to lead Brazil onto the world stage. Use your reputation as a patron of artists, scientists, and engineers to draw the greatest minds to our fertile home. For it is in the lush rainforests, teeming with life, that your people thrive. Watch them in the Carnival as they dance the samba in celebration of your great feats, Pedro the Magnanimous.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_PERICLES: Your mastery of the spoken word is a gift of great value, silver-tongued Pericles, leader of the Greeks. Through it you can attract the devotion of a league of states, surrounding yourself with their glory. Establish cultural sites along the rocky shores of Greece to unite your people behind your strong governance.  If all goes well the Sirens will sing of the Age of Pericles!
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_PETER_GREAT: Embrace the chill winds of the Motherland, Tsar Peter. Your fascination with science and culture is a gift, and you will learn much from your Grand Embassies to foreign lands. Under your rule, Russia will surely flourish and spread, absorbing all that lies around it, perhaps creating the greatest land empire seen on this earth.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_PHILIP_II: All Spain stands ready to answer your prayers, devout King Philip II.  From your palace at El Escorial you can send forth your followers: missionaries, apostles, and conquistadors ready to strike out across the seas to spread the good word about your most holy empire.  May the treasures they uncover fuel your quest to unite the world under one faith and one empire, making you truly the Most Catholic king.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_QIN: In your people lies your greatest strength, Emperor Qin Shi Huang. From all over the world, others will come to gaze upon the great walls and towering wonders of your united China. May the hands of your men never blister as they work hard and fast to raise the most impressive structures that the world will ever know. Protect them well, and you will forever be immortalized.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_SALADIN: The marriage of science and religion is a delicate balancing act, but one that you have mastered, Saladin. Your quest for knowledge is noble, and your people have a deep respect for you. But you need not rush into the unknown. Given time, the answers to life’s most puzzling questions will find their way back to Arabia.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_TOMYRIS: All people will tremble with fear and respect for you, great warrior Queen Tomyris. For it is from the back of your stallion that you shall look upon and lead the Scythian people. Great epics will be told of the horse warriors that ride forth from the steppe, and at the front line of every battle - they will find you. Ride on, fierce queen, and may your friends be true just as your enemies falter.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_TRAJAN: Cast your net wide, oh Trajan, emperor of mighty Rome. Your legions stand at the ready to march out and establish the largest empire the world has ever seen. If you can truly get all roads to lead to Rome, yours will be an empire of great riches and luxuries.  Surely then our citizens will proclaim you as their best ruler, the Optimus Princeps.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_T_ROOSEVELT: And so it is upon your broad shoulders, Theodore Roosevelt, to charge forth and lead your people on their great adventure. Use your military might to give the peoples of your homeland the square deal they so desperately deserve. Surely you will raise America into the limelight and attract visitors from across the oceans just to see your lands. Bully for you, Mr. President.
en_US.LOC_LOADING_INFO_LEADER_VICTORIA: Your Majesty the Queen Victoria of England, extend your reach beyond your borders and across the face of the globe.  Worry not over the possibility of defeat for your loyal redcoats and overwhelming navy will surely carry the day. With your calm and steady touch you can bring all lands under England's sway, establishing a true Pax Britannica.

en_US.LOC_PBC_OVERVIEW_DESC: Play By Cloud is an asynchronous multiplayer format where all players take their turns on a common savegame, which is stored on a hosted server. This is a more modern version of “passing the savegame,” which was the ancient practice of sharing a floppy disk with a common save file between friends (if you are unfamiliar with the concept of a “floppy disk,” please ask a respected adult of venerable age).[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]A Play By Cloud game may last a long time (on the order of days or weeks) as each player takes his or her turn at a time that is convenient to them. You will receive notifications when it is your turn to play. You may see a Steam notification if Steam is active, or you may use the webhooks. Webhooks are a generic message format that the technically-inclined can integrate into other messaging services, email, or Internet of Things devices.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]In asynchronous multiplayer, it is considered courteous to take your turn at your earliest possible convenience to keep the game moving. In ancient times, players were morally obligated to protect the floppy disk from corruption, with unscrupulous players resorting to “losing” the savegame when in an untenable situation. Play By Cloud eliminates such rascally behavior.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_BUILDINGS_PAGE_BUILDING_CVS_SW: The Swiss Confederation is divided into 26 cantons, each of which has its own constitution and assembly in the form of a Cantonal Parlament, or 'Kantonsparlament' in German. The cantons exercise broad authority, possessing all powers not specifically given to the federal government.

The Swiss Confederation consists of some 3,000 communes, which are responsible for public utilities and roads and, like the cantons, are largely autonomous. From the multiplicity of small communal republics stem a special quality to each and, paradoxically, a basis of national unity, for each citizen treasures and supports the freedom of the commune, a shared conviction that unites a citizen with the rest of the population in a way that transcends differences of language and of party.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_BUILDINGS_PAGE_LEADER_BUILDING: Very little remains of Phoenician architecture. Even less remains of this civilopedia.

Okay, fine. Phoenician burial practices varied from city to city, as Phoenicia is more of a catch-all term for a bunch of maritime cities that worshiped the same-ish gods and had similar trading and government structures anyways. One type of grave that is commonly seen across Phoenician colonies is the Shaft Tomb, frequently used for Royals. Most of the tomb is underground, with a sarcophagus laid in a subterranean gallery. Then, this tomb is sealed with some coverstone, until some wayward archaeologist millennia later uncovers it. Ahiram's tomb, along with four other very important sarcophagi, were uncovered in a mudslide in modern Byblos, which lead to severe damage on his sarcophagus. Ahiram\�s sarcophagus in particular was inscribed with a curse meant to protect Byblos, though evidently it did not protect his tomb from being ransacked and robbed blind by graverobbers.

It�s suspected that perhaps the Phoenicians, being originally colonies of Egypt, developed these styles of burial as the more economical version of the Pharaonic burial in Egypt (because who can really afford to build gigantic pyramids everywhere?). It seems that the Phoenicians influenced the Egyptians in their own right, as later Egyptian tombs also featured shafts and underground graves.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_CIVILIZATIONS_PAGE_CIVILIZATIO: Extending well into the western zone of the Southeast Asian archipelago, the Malay Peninsula has long constituted a critical link between the mainland and the islands of Southeast Asia. Because Malaysia itself is divided between the two regions, the history of the country can be understood only within a broad geographic context. The Strait of Malacca, narrowly separating the peninsula from the archipelago, has been a crossroads for peoples, cultures, and trade passing through or taking root in both areas. Influences from China, India, the Middle East, and, later, Europe followed the maritime trade. Peninsular Malaysia and the two states of East Malaysia, Sarawak and Sabah, have shared many historical patterns, but each region also has developed in unique ways.

Malaysia developed an international reputation as the home of renowned seafarers. As its reputation grew, however, Malaysia became increasingly exposed to cultural influences from surrounding powers. Small Malay kingdoms started to appear in the 2nd or 3rd century CE, a time when Indian traders and priests began traveling the maritime routes, bringing with them Indian concepts of religion, government, and the arts. Over many centuries the peoples of the region, especially those within the royal courts, synthesized Indian and indigenous ideas, making selective use of Indian models in shaping their political and cultural patterns.

Alam Melayu, or ‘The Malay World’, is a concept and expression derived from varied interpretations of Malayness largely based on the prevalent Malay cultural influence, manifested through the spread of Malay language in Southeast Asia as observed by different colonial powers during the Age of Discovery. Between the 7th and 13th centuries many of the region’s small, often prosperous maritime trading states came under the loose control of Srivijaya, the great Indianized empire based in Sumatra. At various times, other Indianized powers of Southeast Asia including the Khmer empire based at Angkor, the Tai kingdom of Ayutthaya, and the Majapahit empire centred in eastern Java, also claimed suzerainty in the region. These early cultural forces in Malaysia left a living legacy, traces of which are still evident in the political ideas, social structures, rituals, language, arts, and other traditions of Malay Muslims.

The Chronicon Helveticum is one of the oldest accounts of the early history of the Swiss Confederation. It plays an important part in the historiography of Switzerland, since it contains copies of roughly 50 documents which have not survived in any other form. In terms of content, there is particular interest in representing the long-established independence of the Swiss population, the struggle between empire and papacy, the crusades, and a large number of other issues concerning Swiss cities, dioceses and monasteries.

Switzerland’s history is one of a medieval defensive league formed during a time and in an area lacking imperial authority. The different cantons (traditionally called Orte in German) were to a large extent independent states that remained united through the shared defense of liberty, which was understood as the protection of imperial privileges and franchises.

Unlike similar confederations like the Hanseatic and Swabian leagues, and despite endemic internal strife after the Reformation in the 16th century, the Swiss Confederation survived the formation of (princely) modern states without adapting to it. With Venice, Genoa, and the Netherlands, the confederation formed the republican exception in Europe, and it developed political structures less as a unified nation than on the level of the 13 cantons that the Swiss Confederation comprised.

A product of the European balance of power and, after 1499, attacked only once in 1798, Switzerland has enjoyed peace for most of its existence and was spared from two world wars in the 20th century when the gradually developed concept of “armed neutrality” was respected by its neighbours. Economic prosperity largely followed as Switzerland adapted to the Industrial Revolution and the growth of international finance markets. It stands today as one of the wealthiest nations in the world.

Argentina is a federal republic located in southeastern South America. Covering most of the Southern Cone, it is bordered by Bolivia and Paraguay to the north, Brazil to the northeast, Uruguay and the Atlantic Ocean to the east, Chile to the west and the waters of the Drake Passage to the south.

Argentina is derived from the Latin argentum ("silver"). La Plata Basin does not have any sources of silver, but the first Spanish conquerors arrived in the area following rumors of the existence of silver mountains, hence the name.

The first use of the name Argentina can be traced to La Argentina, a 1602 poem by Martín del Barco Centenera. Although this name for the La Plata Basin was already in common usage by the 18th century, the area was formally called Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata, and United Provinces of the Río de la Plata after independence.

The culture of Argentina is as varied as the country's geography and is composed of a mix of ethnic groups. Modern Argentine culture has been largely influenced by European immigration, although there are lesser elements of Amerindian and African influences, particularly in the fields of music and art. Buenos Aires, its cultural capital, is largely characterized by both the prevalence of people of European descent, and of conscious imitation of European styles in architecture.Museums, cinemas, and galleries are abundant in all the large urban centers, as well as traditional establishments such as literary bars, or bars offering live music of a variety of genres.

The music of Argentina is known mostly for the tango, which developed in Buenos Aires and surrounding areas, as well as Montevideo, Uruguay. Folk, pop and classical music are also popular, and Argentine artists like Mercedes Sosa and Atahualpa Yupanqui contributed greatly to the development of the nueva canción. Argentine rock has also led to a defiant rock scene in Argentina.

Little is known about the enigmatic city now called Teotihuacan � not even its real name. The term itself only came from Aztec squatters, meaning �Birthplace of the Gods�, or �Place where Men become Gods� (actually, not even this is 100% clear. It�s possible that the name of the place in Nahuatl is �Teohuacan�, which can mean �City of the Sun� or �Birthplace of the Sun�). The identity of its true founders has been lost to history, and all that remains are the monumental ruins of the enormous city they built and a legend even bigger than that. As a word of warning, what will follow will be incredibly convoluted, long, and represents a five-year-deep rabbit hole (or sink hole?) that I tumbled down, and still can�t make heads or tails of much of it. In addition, there is still a lot of scholarship going on, and knowing my luck there�s going to be a finding like next week or something that changes everything. So, yeah. Have fun.

Recently, Teotihuacan has come under threat of the development of Mexico City. Thankfully, police raids put a stop to that, and excavations continue to try and unravel the unknowable mysteries of the Birthplace of the Gods.

The history of the settlement dates back to 600 BC, though it really picks up around 200 BC. It can also be divided into four or five phases� though there was also a pre-phase. In its origins, it seems that Teotihuacan was involved in a contest of power with a few other cities, most notably Cuicuilco. During the period of around 600 BC to 200 BC, both Cuicuilco and Teotihuacan had a comparable population of around 20,000 inhabitants each. But, it seems that a number of eruptions of the Xitle and Popocatepetl volcanos covered Teotihuacan�s farmland in a layer of fertile ashes, but Cuicuilco and its farmlands in a layer of very unfertile lava. The survivors flocked to Teotihuacan and its springs, which helped kick-start the city�s development.

Which leads to Period I, from 200BC to the turn of the millennium. Here in the timeline, Teotihuacan evolved from a farming settlement into a true city. The earliest buildings of the city date to this era, and many ethnicities from around Mesoamerica began to take note of the city. It is believed that this is when much of the faith of the city began to take root, giving rise to the earliest forms of the Storm God (early Tlaloc), the Feathered Serpent (early Quetzalcoatl), the War Serpent (also Quetzalcoatl?), the Flayed God (Xip Totec), and the principal deity the Great Goddess (unclear, but associated with spiders).

The first half of period II, sometimes called the Tzacualli phase is when things really started taking off, which ranges from 1 AD to around the year 150 AD. The economic pull of the city brought new immigrants and growth in, which caused the city�s population to explode to 80,000 people. These people allowed for the first great monuments to be built, especially the Temple of the Feathered Serpent and the Ciudadela complex. Scholars believe that this complex was sort of a monument to warfare and autocracy (which also doesn�t jive to me? Explanation will follow in the next paragraph), where sacrifices would take place. Over two hundred sacrifices of people were identified, all of which presumed to be the elites and warriors of Teotihuacan rather than captives of opposing armies. This is also the earliest appearance of Quetzalcoatl in all of Mesoamerica. Beneath this pyramid is a tunnel that had to be investigated by robot in 2010, which lead (after a lot of roving around) to a subchamber which MAY represent a microcosm of the Teotihuacano universe, or maybe a representation of the underworld or something. It was very strange and confusing and almost all theories about it are entirely speculation.

The second half of period II, sometimes called the Miccaotl phase from 150AD to 377AD, was one of reorganization and more building of monuments. It seems that the Temple of the Feathered Serpent fell in importance during this period, which some scholars have interpreted to mean that the city had been reorganized governmentally to be less militant and more collective-driven and bureaucratic. Other scholars believe that that is bogus and is a result of the first scholars putting their own hopes and dreams onto the past. This theory also states that the inhabitants of the Feathered Serpent Complex were exiled from Teotihuacan, and went on to conquer the Maya two hundred years later� but again, this is unlikely.

However, as the city expanded, it is very likely that some political reorganization was in order! It is likely that the Temple of the Feathered Serpent fell in importance compared to new construction around the early 300s AD. The Miccaotl phase saw the construction of the Pyramids of the Sun and Moon, as well as the aforementioned Miccaotl � the famous Avenue of the Dead. This boulevard was aligned in such a way that it corresponded to the 260-day-calendar of Mesoamerica, but also lined up with Cerro Gordo, a mountain with significance to the Storm God. During this period, the trade routes of Mesoamerica began to coalesce at Teotihuacan � a city of 100,000 is an excellent place to do business, and the end-point of a pilgrimage is an even better one.

The year 378 changed everything, but the evidence of this comes not from Teotihuacan, but from the Maya world around 1000 kilometres away. 378 was the beginning year of when Siyaj K�ak�, also known as Fire is Born, was supposedly sent by the Spearthrower Owl to conquer the Maya. Tikal was toppled, and Spearthrower Owl�s son was put in place, and a number of other cities around there fell in a two-year period. At least, this is how the story goes. More on that in the Spearthrower Owl Civilopedia, but this is why Teotihuacan becoming less militant rather than more doesn�t seem to make much sense. 378 seems to be the first year of Period III, when Teotihuacan enters its classic period and really starts flexing its muscles.

The Classic Period lasted from the Campaign of Fire is Born (ending in 380AD) to around the year 650. This is where the city reached its absolute maximum in terms of population � upwards of between 125,000 and 200,000 people � roughly half of everyone in the valley of Mexico lived within its borders. This period also saw renovations of old monuments with new decorations � clad in brilliant burgundy and jade, coated in magnificent but mysterious murals (and unfortunately completed unannotated by script of any kind), and with Teotihuacan�s iconic talud-tablero architecture, mimicked often in the Maya sites it bullied into submission. The military of Teotihuacan had been used to make sure that other city-states would send its tribute to Teotihuacan, and that trade would be properly directed to this city. However, it seems that this period also had a rise in inequality. The city�s class structure seemed to have stratified into three-ish groups � high elites, intermediate elites, and laborers. These laborers were not just the farmers, but also the skilled craftsman, and would live in the outer portions of the city. It seems that during this period, most of the inner city was gentrified. These outer portions also were associated with incredibly high infant mortality. It's a tale as old as time: the big city had even bigger problems, and its golden age wasn't so gold for anyone.

Which finally leads to the last period, Period IV. It�s unclear which order of catastrophes occurred for Teotihuacan, but it was around this time that many of the buildings of the city were burned, and many of its sculptures shattered. The most prominent theory is that what set it off was a series of droughts and climate changes occurred in 535-536 which really set things off. Funnily enough, these changes may have been triggered by the same thing that caused Teotihuacan�s rise in the first place � a volcanic eruption, this time of the Ilopango volcano. Teotihuacan was unable to properly support its military, and thus there was a retreat of Teotihuacan�s armies, followed by a slow degrading of its trade powers. This could have resulted in a malnutrition, unrest, and famine. Seeing weakness, new upstart centers of Cholula, Xochicalco, and Cacaxtla began to jockey for status in the power void. They may have even allied and conspired to weaken Teotihuacan even further. All the while, Teotihuacan starved. The fall finally came at some point between 650 and 750, when major civic centers along the Avenue of the Dead were burned and sacked. Teotihuacan was abandoned soon after.

The Thule (Pronounced 'Too-lee') Peoples were ancestors of the modern Inuit who inhabited the northern territories of modern Canada, Alaska and Greenland. Developing first in 10th century Alaska, they stretched across Canada and into Greenland in the next 300 years, displacing and dominating the preceding Dorset cultures.

Though they only began truly prospering in the 10th century, Thule Tradition approximately began in 200 B.C.E in the Bering Strait, though this estimate varies greatly. The strong maritime-hunter and artistic tradition of the Thule first took shape here, in what became known as the Old Bering Sea stage of Thule tradition. Decorated ivory harpoon heads and remains of Umiaks (large skinned boats used for whaling), and various other tools made of ivory and polished slate are discovered from this time. Specifically, innovations in the form of harpoon-mounted ice picks, toggling harpoon, sophisticated tools for seal and walrus-hunting, and their mastery of dogs helped the early Thule.

Following the Old Bering Sea stage was the Punuk stage, where the Thule were able to dominate the Dorset culture due to their more advanced technologies. The Thule thrived in their vast new territories, and the seal and walrus-society transitioned into the whaling-centered culture the Thule became known for. The ideal quarry was the Bowhead whale, primarily due to slow swimming and sleeping near the surface. The Bowhead's blubber, meat, bones, and skins became important and eventually essential to Thule life. These necessary resources were carved into the tools needed for hunting, the frames for their whalebone houses, and their beautiful relics.

Thule culture moved into a cycle of wintering in large semi-subterranean houses made of wood and whalebone, to summer life in skin huts. Teams of experienced whalers in multiple umiaks, lead by a prestigious veteran captain known as the umialik would go out and whale in narrow ice leads and then the open sea during the fall. Though open-sea whaling was dangerous, the expert hunters and boatmen developed bone armor, archery, even more advanced hunting tools, and expert techniques to mitigate the dangers.

Around the year 800 A.D., Thule culture divided into the western half in Alaska and more mainland Canada, and the eastern half in Greenland and the High Arctic Seas. The Eastern half became known as the Birnirk stage, who transitioned on their own through the Early, Middle, and Late Birnirk stages. Gradually, harpoon head and arrow styles changed from being highly decorated ivory points to unembellished versions made of antler.

Meanwhile, the eastern Punuk entered the Classic Thule era from the years 1100 to 1400 A.D. They began using iron tools derived from meteoric resources or trade from Norse contact, but ultimately had a very limited supply of iron. The metal was used for carving, but the Thule’s artistic tendencies continued to decline.

Thule faith developed into a form of Animism and Shamanism. Priest-healers known as Angakkuit helped communities in times of crisis, especially during whaling and marine scarcity. The harshness of life in the icy north made the people live in constant fear of unseen and supernatural forces, with some motifs being around protectors or guardians, and others around overcoming supernatural obstacles. They also believed that all things have an anirniq – a spirit – that are borrowed from the sky around them, and persist after death and are free to take revenge.

Postclassical Thule was a period of decline due to climate changes and lack of whales – settlements were now forced to use subsistence strategies of land-based hunting or fishing. The decreasing temperatures of the little Ice Age caused the whale-hunting season to shorten and whaling efforts were finally abandoned by the 17th century.

Thule tradition made contact with European society before their demise. Though they had already contacted the Norse, who called them skrælingr, they encountered Basque whalers and later French and English explorers. Plagues killed the Thule en masse, and material wealth disrupted the Thule way of life as they began to transform into the Inuit society. During a time when their main source of food was rapidly depleting, the impact of European colonization was devastating and ultimately lethal to the culture. The last trappings of the Thule culture died out by the year 1850, being replaced entirely by modern Inuit in the British Canadian colonies.

Finland is a sovereign state in Northern Europe. The country has land borders with Sweden to the northwest, Norway to the north, and Russia to the east. To the south is the Gulf of Finland with Estonia on the opposite side. Finland is a Nordic country and, together with Scandinavia, is situated in the geographical region of Fennoscandia.

Finland was inhabited when the last ice age ended, approximately 9000 BCE. The first settlers left behind artifacts that present characteristics shared with those found in Estonia, Russia, and Norway. The earliest people were hunter-gatherers, using stone tools. The first pottery appeared in 5200 BCE, when the Comb Ceramic culture was introduced. The arrival of the Corded Ware culture in southern coastal Finland between 3000 and 2500 BCE may have coincided with the start of agriculture. The Bronze Age and Iron Age were characterised by extensive contacts with other cultures in the Fennoscandian and Baltic regions and the sedentary farming inhabitation increased towards the end of Iron Age. At the time Finland had three main cultural areas, Southwest Finland, Tavastia and Karelia, as reflected in contemporary jewellery.

From the late 13th century, Finland gradually became an integral part of Sweden through the crusades and the Swedish part-colonisation of coastal Finland, a legacy reflected in the prevalence of the Swedish language and its official status. In 1809, Finland was incorporated into the Russian Empire as the autonomous Grand Duchy of Finland. Following the 1917 Russian Revolution, Finland declared itself independent. In 1918, the fledgling state was divided by civil war, with the Bolshevik-leaning Red Guard supported by the equally new Soviet Russia, fighting the White Guard, supported by the German Empire. After a brief attempt to establish a kingdom, the country became a republic. During World War II, the Soviet Union sought repeatedly to occupy Finland, with Finland losing parts of Karelia, Salla, Kuusamo, Petsamo and some islands, but retaining independence.

Finland was a relative latecomer to industrialisation, remaining a largely agrarian country until the 1950s. After World War II, the Soviet Union demanded war reparations from Finland not only in money but also in material, such as ships and machinery. This forced Finland to industrialise. It rapidly developed an advanced economy while building an extensive welfare state based on the Nordic model, resulting in widespread prosperity and one of the highest per capita incomes in the world.

The culture of Finland combines indigenous heritage, as represented for example by the country's Uralic national language Finnish and the sauna, with common Nordic, Russian and European culture. Because of its history and geographic location Finland has been influenced by the adjacent areas, various Finnic and Baltic peoples as well as the former dominant powers of Sweden and Russia.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_DISTRICS_PAGE_DISTRICT_LEU_ARR: Arrabales were neighborhoods built on Argentina, usually linked to the working class of the country. It is within Arrabales where Tango was born. The tango’s roots make it a song for marginalized people. The tango’s vibrant beat fuses traditions of European immigrants, South-American natives and descendants of African slaves. The tango is the product of a concrete historical process: a biological and cultural mix that took place in the urban suburbs of Buenos Aires from the end of the nineteenth century until the 1960s. The soul of Buenos Aires is expressed through this song. The tango reflects its inhabitants’ way of being and its folklore.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_DISTRICTS_PAGE_DISTRICT_CVS_MA: An important trading and knowledge center since the seventh century, the inhabitants of the Malay peninsular took advantage of a strategic location in the Strait of Malacca that made it one of the known world's most important centers of maritime commerce.

The seaport (or 'Dermaga') town of Malacca was used mainly by merchants as a major transshipment port on the route between India and China, and thus became the target of blockades and attacks from various European nations that wanted to bring Malacca under their own control. Though Malacca changed hands between the Portuguese, the Dutch and British over the coming centuries, the Strait that still bears its namesake remains one of the most important maritime shipping lanes today.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_DISTRICTS_PAGE_DISTRICT_LEU_ES: Estancias, or ranches, play a huge part in Argentina's culture, economy and history. In the early days these establishments were responsible for making Argentina one of the biggest meat and grain producers in the world. These enormous ranches dotted the entire countryside and are to this day where the best steaks in the world come from. During the conflicts with the Mapuche and Pehuelche Estancias also served as important defense points for the frontier.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_DISTRICTS_PAGE_DISTRICT_LIME_T: Technically speaking, a Pochtecatl refers explicitly to a professional, long-distance trader in the Aztec Empire, which originated almost a thousand years after Teotihuac�n fell, but Pochteca may also used more generally for any Mesoamerican trader. And Teotihuac�n had quite a connection with its traders! An entire quarter (Calpulli in Nahuatl, or Barrio in Spanish � this was a big issue in the development of the mod) of the city was dedicated to the these foreign traders that would become key to Teotihuac�n�s success.

Teotihuac�n lived and died by its trade routes. Much of the power of this city came from its ability to control and redirect the trade routes of Mesoamerica into this one location, making it the largest and most glorious city of the new world until the rise of Tenochtitlan. The most important trade good of the city was manufactured obsidian, which was refined and sculpted in laboratories of the city-state. Art, masks, figurines, ornaments, and especially blades and knife handles were made in these workshops � a monopoly that Teotihuac�n had carefully cultivated during its period. Other industries in the city included various types of pottery and jewelry, and the city of that size would have required extensive food imports.

These trade routes also contributed to the awesome size of the city. Teotihuac�n was home to many ethnicities, which makes identifying the original ethnicity all the harder. Many of these ethnic groups would have their own neighborhoods and would use their own writing system � Zapotec, Maya, Mixtec, Totonac, and even Toltec (which is a word in Nahuatl which may translate to �craftsman of the highest caliber.� Definitely totally coincidental to the number of crafts occurring in the city. Totally. Yeah.) The Pochteca of the city had a particularly unique quarter, which had circular residences compared to the normal rectangular architecture of Mesoamerica. More curiously, some strontium analysis on bodies found in the barrio show that some people (not all! Some of them were born-and-bred Teotihuacanos) were originally from the Gulf Coast region.

Teotihuac�n used its religious importance and awesome architecture to attract trade routes, with any trade routes and city-states that tried to avoid the city soon receiving a friendly visit by nearby extremely-well-armed soldiers, but also used those very trade routes to shore up its religious importance. Many of the gods of Teotihuac�n were exported to other ethnicities by this means, becoming the Quetzalcoatl and Tlaloc we all know and love. However, it seems that when Teotihuac�n�s military grip on the trade routes of the region slipped in the mid fifth-century AD, and it was not long after that the city would fall.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_FEATURES_PAGE_FEATURE_BARRINGE: The Barringer Crater is a huge meteorite crater located in Arizona, in the United States of America. The crater is 1,200 meters (4,000 feet) in diameter, and scientists believe that it was created some 50,000 years ago when the site was hit by a large nickel-iron meteorite weighing, at time of impact, 160,000 tons and moving at perhaps 44,000 kilometers per hour (27,000 mph).
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_FEATURES_PAGE_FEATURE_BIOLUMIN: The Bioluminescent Bay (also known as Puerto Mosquito, or Mosquito Bay), is considered the best example of a bioluminescent bay in the United States and is listed as a national natural landmark, one of five in Puerto Rico. The luminescence in the bay is caused by a micro-organism, the dinoflagellate Pyrodinium bahamense, which glows whenever the water is disturbed, leaving a trail of neon blue..

A combination of factors creates the necessary conditions for bioluminescence: red mangrove trees surround the water, a complete lack of modern development around the bay, the water is cool enough and deep enough, and a small channel to the ocean keeps the dinoflagellates in the bay. This small channel was created artificially, being the result of attempts by the occupants of Spanish ships to choke off the bay from the ocean. The Spanish believed that the bioluminescence they encountered there while first exploring the area, was the work of the devil and tried to block ocean water from entering the bay by dropping huge boulders in the channel. The Spanish only succeeded in preserving and increasing the luminescence in the now isolated bay.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_FEATURES_PAGE_FEATURE_CERRO_DE: Located in southern Bolivia, the mountain of Potosi produced nearly all of the silver mined by the Spanish during their imperial days. Once removed from the mountain, it was taken by llama and mule to the coast where it was then loaded onto treasure ships sailing back to Europe. Nearly 41,000 tons of pure silver were mined over the course of 200 years, 8,200 of which went directly to the Spanish crown. After 1800, the main silver mines were depleted, but the mining of Potosi still continues today - some for silver but now mostly for tin.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_FEATURES_PAGE_FEATURE_DALLOL_C: Dallol is a cinder cone volcano in the Danakil Depression, northeast of the Erta Ale Range in Ethiopia. It has been formed by the intrusion of basaltic magma into Miocene salt deposits and subsequent hydrothermal activity. Phreatic eruptions took place in 1926, forming Dallol Volcano while numerous other eruption craters dot the salt flats nearby. These craters are the lowest known subaerial volcanic vents in the world, at 45 m (150 ft) or more below sea level.

Numerous hot springs are discharging brine and acidic liquid here. Small, widespread, temporary geysers produce cones of salt. The Dallol deposits include significant bodies of potash found directly at the surface. The term 'Dallol' was coined by the Afar people and means 'dissolution' or 'disintegration', describing a landscape of green acid ponds (pH-values less than 1) and iron oxide, sulfur and salt desert plains.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_FEATURES_PAGE_FEATURE_GIBRALTA: Gibraltar is a peninsula containing a remarkable rock formation at the mouth of the Mediterranean Sea. Captured from Spain by the English and Dutch in 1704 and ceded to England in 1713, Gibraltar has been a British possession ever since (much to the annoyance of Spain, which wants it back). Commanding the entrance to the Atlantic from the Mediterranean, Gibraltar has been a major British naval base for three hundred years. Most of Gibraltar is covered by the 'Rock', a huge formation of shale, sandstone and limestone thrust up by the unimaginable power of plate tectonics. The Rock stands some 430 meters (1400 feet) in height. At one time Gibraltar was a massive fortification allowing Britain to dominate the narrow Mediterranean-Atlantic passage, but today the island is more of a nature preserve and tourist destination than it is a military base.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_FEATURES_PAGE_FEATURE_GRAND_ME: The Grand Mesa is a large geologic formation in Colorado, the United States of America. Rising some 1,500 meters (5,000 feet) above the surrounding territory and with an area of 1300 square kilometers (500 square miles), it is the largest mesa in the world. The Grand Mesa has a layer of volcanic basalt on top, which resists erosion. It did not so much rise into the air, as it remained at its original height, as the surrounding terrain was eroded by the action of the Colorado and Gunnison rivers.  The Grand Mesa National Forest (originally called Battlement Mesa Forest Reserve) was created by Benjamin Harrison on December 24, 1892. It was the third forest reserve created in United States.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_FEATURES_PAGE_FEATURE_KAILASH_: The sacred peak of Mount Kailash, found in the Himalayas of Tibet, is cherished by a number of religions, particularly the followers of Hinduism. It is believed to be the home of Lord Shiva, who dwells on the mountain in a state of eternal bliss. Mount Kailash is said to be among the most difficult of all religious pilgrimages, as the harsh conditions dissuade many would-be pilgrims, and the mountain is not accessible by any forms of modern transportation.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_FEATURES_PAGE_FEATURE_KRAKATOA: Krakatoa is a volcanic island located in Indonesia, between the islands of Java and Sumatra. The volcano exploded violently in August, 1883 with a force equivalent to 13,000 times the power of the Hiroshima nuclear bomb. The blast is widely regarded as the loudest sound ever recorded. The eruption destroyed over half of the island, and was heard in parts of Australia, some 3,200 kilometers (2,000 miles) away. Some 37,000 people were killed by the eruption and subsequent tsunamis. The volcano has been emitting lava steadily for the past eighty years, rebuilding the cone at a rate of about 5 meters per year (15 feet per year).
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_FEATURES_PAGE_FEATURE_LAKE_VIC: With a surface area over 26,000 square miles (68,800 km²), Lake Victoria is the largest lake in Africa, the second largest freshwater lake on Earth, and the largest tropical lake in the world. Two large rivers leave the lake, the White Nile and the Katonga. The first historical records of the lake come from Arab traders seeking gold, ivory and other commodities from the natives as they pushed inland from the coast. The search by European explorers for the source of the Nile led to the discovery of the lake by the Englishman John Speke in 1858 AD, who named it after the then British monarch.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_FEATURES_PAGE_FEATURE_LENCOIS_: Located in Maranhão state in northeastern Brazil, Lençóis Maranhenses National Park is composed of 380,000 acres of rolling sand dunes that flood with freshwater during the rainy season. The park is home to a range of species, four of which are endangered, and due to its unique physical properties it has become a popular destination for ecotourists.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_FEATURES_PAGE_FEATURE_MOSI_OA_: The Mosi-oa-Tunya, otherwise known as Victoria Falls, is among the most spectacular waterfalls in the world. The Zambezi River, which is more than 2 kilometers wide at this point, plunges noisily down a series of basalt gorges and raises an iridescent mist that can be seen more than 50 km away. Its name, which translates to 'The Smoke Which Thunders', comes from the Kololo or Lozi language used throughout Zambia and in parts of Zimbabwe, though it is more commonly known worldwide as Victoria Falls due to Scottish missionary and explorer, David Livingstone, who is perhaps most famous for giving a name to a waterfall that already had one.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_FEATURES_PAGE_FEATURE_MOTLATSE: The Motlatse Canyon is a significant natural feature of South Africa, located in Mpumalanga, and forming the northern part of the Drakensberg escarpment. Located in the Blyde River Canyon Nature Reserve, it is 25 kilometers in length and is, on average, around 750 meters deep, sporting some of the deepest precipitous cliffs of any canyon on the planet.

While it is difficult to compare canyons world-wide, Blyde River Canyon is one of the largest canyons on Earth, and it may be the largest green canyon due to its lush subtropical foliage. It supports a large diversity of flora and fauna, including numerous fish and antelope species as well as hippos, crocodiles and every primate species that may be seen in south Africa, making it a very popular region for tourism.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_FEATURES_PAGE_FEATURE_NAMIB_CH: The Namib is a coastal desert in southern Africa, whose name is of Nama origin and means 'vast place'. The Namib stretches for more than 2,000km along the Atlantic coasts of Angola, Namibia, and South Africa. Having endured arid, or semi-arid conditions for roughly 55-80 million years, the Namib may be the oldest desert in the world, containing some of the world's driest regions. Owing to its aridity, the Namib is almost totally uninhabited except for a small number of scattered settlements, which have historically served as trading posts for the routes of traders and missionaries that cross the desert.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_FEATURES_PAGE_FEATURE_OLD_FAIT: Old Faithful is a geyser found in Yellowstone National Park, in Wyoming, US. First seen by Europeans in 1870 (and by natives some 10,000 years before that), Old Faithful was thus named because of the regularity of its eruption. The geyser shoots a column of boiling water to a height of some 30-50 meters (100-175 feet) every 60-90 minutes (the interval determined by the ferocity of the previous eruption). Geysers occur when subterranean water hits magma (molten rock). The water is instantly turned to steam, which rushes out the nearest available opening at tremendously high pressure. Old Faithful and the other 250 geysers in Yellowstone are enjoyed by some three million visitors each year.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_FEATURES_PAGE_FEATURE_OUNIANGA: Lakes of Ounianga are a series of eighteen interconnected lakes in the hyper arid Ennedi region of the Sahara desert, occupying a basin in the mountains of West Tibesti and Ennedi East. It constitutes an exceptional natural landscape of great beauty with striking colours and shapes. The saline, hyper saline and freshwater lakes are supplied by groundwater and are found in two groups 40 km apart. Ounianga Kebir comprises four lakes, the largest of which, Yoan, covers an area of 358 ha and is 27 m deep. Its highly saline waters only sustain algae and some microorganisms. The second group, Ounianga Serir, comprises fourteen lakes separated by sand dunes. Floating reeds cover almost half the surface of these lakes reducing evaporation. Lake Teli has the largest surface area but is less than 10 m deep. With their high quality freshwater, some of these lakes are home to aquatic fauna, particularly fish.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_FEATURES_PAGE_FEATURE_SALAR_DE: Situated in southwest Bolivia, near the Chilean border and the Atacama Desert, lies Salar de Uyuni; the largest salt flat on Earth at 10,582 square kilometers, roughly 100 times the size of the Bonneville Salt Flats in the United States. The Salar was formed a result of transformations between several prehistoric lakes. Covered by a few meters of salt crust, it has an extraordinary flatness with the average elevation variations within one meter over the entire area of the Salar. The large area, clear skies, and exceptional flatness of the surface make it an ideal object for calibrating the altimeters of Earth observation satellites.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_FEATURES_PAGE_FEATURE_SINAI_CH: Found on the Sinai Peninsula of Egypt, Mount Sinai is among the most revered holy sites recognized by the followers of Judaism, Christianity, and Islam. Mount Sinai is believed to be the location where Moses first received the Ten Commandments from God during the Israelites' exodus from Egypt, making the peak an important site for religious pilgrims from around the world.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_FEATURES_PAGE_FEATURE_SRI_PADA: Towering above Sri Lanka, Sri Pada is a large mountain peak with an unusually conical shape that is held sacred by a number of religions for the footprint found at its peak. The footprint, a large depression found in a rock formation on the summit, has been attributed to Buddha, Shiva, and the biblical figure Adam, leading to a reverence among followers of Buddhism, Hinduism, and Islam. Each year, thousands of pilgrims trek for hours up the mountain to pay their respects at the holy site.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_FEATURES_PAGE_FEATURE_VREDEFOR: The Vredefort Dome is the largest verified impact crater on Earth, more than 300km across when it was formed. What remains of it is located in the present-day Free State province of South Africa where cultivated agriculture dominates the landscape. The crater is estimated to be over 2 billion years old, with impact taking place in the Paleoproterozoic Era, making it the second-oldest known crater on Earth.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_FEATURES_PAGE_FEATURE_WULINGYU: Wulingyuan is a scenic and historical site in south-central China. It is noted for more than 3,000 quartzite sandstone pillars and peaks, many over 200 meters in height, along with ravines, gorges, pools, lakes, rivers and waterfalls. It features 40 caves and two natural bridges, Xianrenqiao (Bridge of the Immortals) and Tianqiashengkong (Bridge Across the Sky).
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_GOVERNMENTS_PAGE_POLICY_HARD_S: According to the story, around the year 1189 Iron Li developed a new method for hunting foxes which used a ceramic explosive to scare foxes into his nets. The explosive consisted of a ceramic bottle with a mouth, stuffed with gunpowder, and attached with a fuse. Explosive and net were placed at strategic points of places such as watering holes frequented by foxes, and when they got near enough, Iron Li would light the fuse, causing the ceramic bottle to explode and scaring the frightened foxes right into his nets.[NEWLINE]While a fanciful tale, it's not exactly certain why this would cause the development of the iron bomb, given the explosive was made using ceramics, and other materials such as bamboo or even leather would have done the same job, assuming they made a loud enough noise. Nonetheless, the iron bomb made its first appearance in 1221 at the siege of Qizhou (in modern Hubei province), and this time it would be the Jin who possessed the technological advantage. The Song commander Zhao Yurong survived and was able to relay his account for posterity.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_GOVERNMENTS_PAGE_POLICY_SIEGE_: During the Peloponnesian War, one hundred sieges were attempted and fifty-eight ended with the surrender of the besieged area.[NEWLINE]Alexander the Great's army successfully besieged many powerful cities during his conquests. Two of his most impressive achievements in siegecraft took place in the Siege of Tyre and the Siege of the Sogdian Rock. His engineers built a causeway that was originally 60 m (200 ft) wide and reached the range of his torsion-powered artillery, while his soldiers pushed siege towers housing stone throwers and light catapults to bombard the city walls.[NEWLINE]Most conquerors before him had found Tyre, a Phoenician island-city about 1 km from the mainland, impregnable. The Macedonians built a mole, a raised spit of earth across the water, by piling stones up on a natural land bridge that extended underwater to the island, and although the Tyrians rallied by sending a fire ship to destroy the towers, and captured the mole in a swarming frenzy, the city eventually fell to the Macedonians after a seven-month siege. In complete contrast to Tyre, Sogdian Rock was captured by stealthy attack. Alexander used commando-like tactics to scale the cliffs and capture the high ground, and the demoralized defenders surrendered.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_GOVERNMENTS_PAGE_POLICY_TRENCH: Trench warfare is a type of land warfare using occupied fighting lines largely comprising military trenches, in which troops are well-protected from the enemy's small arms fire and are substantially sheltered from artillery. Trench warfare became archetypically associated with the World War I (1914-1918), when the Race to the Sea rapidly expanded trench use on the Western Front starting in September 1914.[NEWLINE]Trench warfare proliferated when a revolution in firepower was not matched by similar advances in mobility, resulting in a gruelling form of warfare in which the defender held the advantage. On the Western Front in 1914-1918, both sides constructed elaborate trench, underground, and dugout systems opposing each other along a front, protected from assault by barbed wire. The area between opposing trench lines (known as "no man's land") was fully exposed to artillery fire from both sides. Attacks, even if successful, often sustained severe casualties.
en_US.LOC_PEDIA_IMPROVEMENTS_PAGE_IMPROVEMENT_: The Thule peoples constructed large semi-subterranean houses called Whalebone Houses. These houses were usually large enough to house eight to ten people, and served as shelter during the brutal polar winters. They varied widely in layout, but all were made half underground with a frame made of wood and whale ivory (shocking, I know). All featured a hearth, presumably because the Thule peoples did not enjoy freezing to death.
